thread_title: FOI/EIR 00211027 — acquisition of land for Llandough Primary School
from: Information Governance Officer, Vale of Glamorgan Council (FoiUnit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk)
subject: FOI request - Case Ref/ 00211027
body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your request for information about Llandough Primary School and your further enquires around whom you within the Information Governance team you have been corresponding with.

You asked

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and, where applicable, the Environmental Information Regulations 2004, I request copies of records relating to the acquisition of the land used for the construction of Llandough Primary School.

Specifically, I request:

■ The transfer deed, conveyance or other legal instrument by which the Council acquired the land.

■ The purchase price or consideration paid for the land.

■ If the land was gifted, transferred at nominal value or below market value, records explaining the basis for that arrangement.

■ Any valuation reports obtained before acquisition.

■ Any agreements, correspondence or meeting minutes between the Council and BP (or any BP subsidiary, trust or associated company) concerning the transfer of the land.

■ Any Cabinet, Committee or Council reports authorising the acquisition.

■ Any planning agreements or obligations connected with the transfer.

If any of the requested information is already publicly available, please provide the relevant links or document references.

You then issued further correspondence requesting:

On 14 July 2026 you acknowledged my FOI/EIR request (Case Ref 00211027) concerning the acquisition of land for Llandough Primary School.

I replied the same day asking for the name of the officer who sent the acknowledgement. I have received no further response or substantive reply.

Our Response

The transfer deed, conveyance or other legal instrument by which the Council acquired the land
The Council holds a conveyance dated 11 June 1965 made between:
1. Lakeside and Llandough Development Company Limited;
2. Western Ground Rents Limited; and
3. The Glamorgan County Council.
A scanned copy of the conveyance and its plan is attached (“the 1965 Conveyance”).

The purchase price or consideration paid for the land
The consideration recorded in the 1965 Conveyance is £16,800.

If the land was gifted, transferred at nominal value or below market value, records explaining the basis of that arrangement
The 1965 Conveyance records a purchase for £16,800. No record has been located within the papers held by Legal Services indicating that the land was gifted or transferred at nominal value or below market value.

Any valuation reports obtained before acquisition
Searches were undertaken with Legal Services and Estates Department. No valuation report relating to the acquisition has been identified. The Council does not hold any valuation report falling within the scope of this request.

Any agreements, correspondence or meeting minutes between the Council and BP, or any BP subsidiary, trust or associated company, concerning the transfer
No agreements, correspondence or meeting minutes between the Council and BP or any BP subsidiary, trust or associated company relating to the acquisition of the land have been identified.

Any Cabinet, Committee or Council reports authorising the acquisition
The Council has not identified any Cabinet, Committee or Council reports within its current records management systems which fall within the scope of your request. Given the age of the acquisition, any surviving historic records may have been transferred to Glamorgan Archives. You may wish to contact Glamorgan Archives directly regarding records from this period.

Any planning agreements or obligations connected with the transfer
No planning agreement or planning obligation connected with the 1965 Conveyance has been identified within the title deeds held by Legal Services or, within the Planning Departments records.

We have considered this aspect of your correspondence under the Freedom of Information Act 2000.
The Council’s Information Governance Team deal with requests on a collective basis and all requests will be considered by different officers. The requests are dealt with via a generic e-mail account so that all officers in the Team can consider correspondence. There are several reasons why the Information Governance Team work in this way. One reason is to ensure that correspondence is considered as soon as possible and to ensure that messages or e-mails are not sent to individuals and overlooked within our systems overall. The information requested is also considered to constitute the personal data of a member of staff and disclosure would amount to disclosure to the world at large. Therefore the Council is unable to provide the name of the individual officer, because it is not considered that there is a lawful basis that would make disclosure fair or necessary in the circumstances. The Council's correspondence is issued on behalf of the authority, and requests for information under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 or the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 are made to the Council as a public authority rather than to individual officers. It is not necessary to know the identity of a particular officer in order to submit a valid request for information.
If you are dissatisfied with the handling of your request, you have the right to ask for an internal review. Internal review requests should be made within 40 working days of the date of receipt of the response to your original letter and should be addressed to:
c/o The Monitoring Officer – Foiunit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

Or by post to The Monitoring Officer, Civic Offices, Holton Road, Barry, CF63 4RU.

thread_title: N610CGV — surviving first-registration records: letter of 30 July 2026 and unanswered follow-ups
subject: 2 of 2 - Unanswered clarification — N610CGV / WA231076 & WA240304 — emails of 26 May, 2–3 June, 30 July and 12 August 2026
body:
Mr Haste,

This supplements my email of 16 September 2026 on N610CGV / WA231076 and WA240304. It is not a complaint, not a request to reopen stage 2, and not a FOIA request. Please treat points 8–14 with points 1–7 as one live enquiry (also your customer-support refs 260812-6561894 and 260812-6565153).

8. 1971 abstract as listed on the DL, versus the document itself

Ms Takeuchi’s letter of 19 April 2026 stated that “an abstract of title listed dated 1971 was lodged” and that the deeds were listed on the form DL. Your 30 July schedule has an A13-DL (WA231076 item 17) but no separate 1971 abstract.

Please confirm:
whether item 17 still lists a 1971 abstract;

if it does, whether the abstract itself is still held, and under which item;

if the abstract is listed but no longer held, when and how it left the file.

9. Form 1E / Form 1C / FR1
Ms Takeuchi referred to certificates on Form FR1. Your 30 July letter identifies Form 1E (30 November 1982, item 13) and, for WA240304, Form 1C (item 11).

Please confirm:
whether an FR1 also survives for either title;
whether 1E and 1C are the first-registration application forms;

whether the wording “not aware of any question or doubt affecting the title” appears on 1E, on 1C, on an FR1, or on none of them.

10. The 31 December 1969 Western Ground Rents conveyance

Ms Takeuchi and Ms Griffiths treated the 31 December 1969 conveyance (Western Ground Rents Ltd to the BP Pension Trust parties) as the root recited in the 1975 and 1982 conveyances. That 1969 deed does not appear as an item on the 30 July schedule.

Please confirm whether the 1969 conveyance:

is held (give title and item number);
was only recited and never lodged; or
was lodged and is no longer held.
11. Paper files and the February 2026 scan
Ms Griffiths wrote on 13 February 2026 that she had “ordered the historic paper files of the first registration” and was awaiting scanning.

Please confirm:
whether those paper files were retrieved and scanned in full;

whether the originals are still held, and where;

whether the 30 July list is the complete surviving set from that retrieval;

the procedure under Land Registration Act 2002 s.66 for inspection of the originals, as distinct from paid OC2 copies.

12. Examiner material already identified
Your 30 July list includes WA240304 item 7: “Application form D23 (inside exam) and letter dated 8 April 1983 from Linklaters & Paines.” That is examiner/requisition material.

Please confirm what the D23 and the 8 April 1983 letter concern, or state that you will not read them and that they should be requested as OC2 items. Identify any other surviving examiner notes, requisitions or file notes for either title.

13. Class of title and cautions at first registration

Please confirm, from the surviving register editions you listed (including WA240304 item 10, 23 February 1983, and WA231076 item 23, 13 January 1984):

the class of title first granted on each title (absolute / possessory / qualified);

whether any caution, notice, restriction or inhibition was entered at or before completion of first registration.

Mr Gill’s letter of 25 May 2026 said no caution was received from my family. I am asking what the register editions themselves show, not for a restatement of that conclusion.

14. Amalgamation
WA231076 item 14 is an application to amalgamate dated 2 February 1987. Please confirm that WA240304 was wholly absorbed into WA231076, or identify any part of the closed title that was not.

subject: FAO: Barry Preservation Society / the Civic Trust
body:
Dear Freedom of Information Officer,

I am researching the 1989 planning application for the development
subsequently known as Church View Close, Llandough-juxta-Penarth.

The planning officer's report records that representations were received
from the *Barry Preservation Society* and the *Civic Trust*, but the report
does not reproduce the substance of those representations.

Please provide copies of all records held by the Council relating to the
representation made by the *Barry Preservation Society* in connection with
that planning application, including:

1. The original letter, objection or representation submitted by the
Barry Preservation Society.
2. Any covering letter, acknowledgement or correspondence concerning its
submission.
3. Any internal Council correspondence referring to or summarising the
Society's representations.
4. Any plans, photographs or supporting material submitted by the
Society.
5. Any correspondence concerning the *retention, preservation,
alteration or demolition of Great House Farm farmhouse*.
6. Any subsequent correspondence between the Council and the Barry
Preservation Society concerning Great House Farm or the development.

I am particularly seeking the Society's *original 1989 comments about Great
House Farm farmhouse*, rather than a later summary of them.

The organisation is referred to in later Vale of Glamorgan Council records
as the *Barry Preservation Society*, including its participation in the
Council's Conservation Area Advisory Group. It also appears in historical
publications as the *Barry Preservation Society and Civic Trust*.

If the original representation is no longer held, please state that
explicitly and provide any surviving reference, file number, minute,
extract or other record that identifies what was submitted and when.

Please search the complete planning file and associated correspondence
rather than relying solely on the published officer report.

Regards,

Sion Buckler

thread_title: Corporate complaint VOG-874631131 — demolition (1988) and planning handling
subject: Great House Farm, Llandough
note: The email as sent repeats its opening and most of its body; it is reproduced exactly as sent.
body:
Customer Relations / Planning Complaints Officer,

I wish to make a formal complaint concerning the Vale of Glamorgan
Council's Dear Customer Relations / Planning Complaints Officer,

I wish to make a formal complaint concerning the Vale of Glamorgan
Council's handling of Great House Farm, Llandough-juxta-Penarth,
particularly the circumstances surrounding its demolition in December 1988
and the subsequent planning process.

Please register this as a formal complaint under the Council's corporate
complaints procedure and provide me with a complaint reference number.

This complaint concerns the Council's administration and exercise of its
planning and heritage responsibilities. It is not intended to constitute an
appeal against a properly made historic planning decision.

1. Great House Farm, Llandough (Cardiff not Cowbridge) was recognised as a
building of historic importance

The planning and archaeological documentation concerning the site
identifies Great House Farm as a building of heritage significance.

In particular, the archaeological material identifies the former building
as a "county treasure" associated with SMR 2038s, while earlier
architectural recording by RCAHMW describes a substantial historic
farmhouse with surviving historic fabric.

The later 1990 archaeological assessment states:

«"Owing to an ownership dispute and the subsequent sudden destruction of
the property in 1988 the building was incompletely understood."»

I regard that statement as highly significant because it records,
contemporaneously with the subsequent planning process, that the building
had been destroyed suddenly and that its archaeological and architectural
history had therefore not been adequately understood or recorded.

2. The Council's apparent failure to take protective action before the 1988
demolition

I ask the Council to investigate what action, if any, its planning and
heritage officers took when Great House Farm was at risk of demolition.

In particular, I ask the Council to establish:

1. Whether the Council knew that Great House Farm was at risk of demolition
before December 1988.

2. Whether the Council received any notification, complaint, application,
correspondence or other warning concerning the proposed demolition.

3. Whether the building had been considered for statutory listing or other
statutory protection.

4. Whether consideration was given to the use of a Building Preservation
Notice or any other available statutory or administrative mechanism capable
of preventing or delaying demolition pending assessment.

5. Whether the Council's heritage officers, planning officers or
archaeological advisers were consulted.

6. Whether any inspection or photographic/architectural record was
undertaken immediately before or after the demolition.

7. Why, given the building's recognised historic significance, the Council
did not secure a comprehensive standing-building record before the building
was lost.

I am not asserting at this stage that a particular statutory power
necessarily had to be exercised. I am asking the Council to investigate
what powers and procedures were available in 1988 and why they were, or
were not, used in this case.

3. The "sudden destruction" of the building requires investigation

The 1990 archaeological assessment expressly attributes the incomplete
understanding of the building to its "subsequent sudden destruction ... in
1988".

I therefore ask the Council to establish from its records:

- the date on which it first became aware of the proposed or actual
demolition;

- the identity of the relevant officers;

- whether the Council received complaints or reports concerning demolition
activity;

- whether any site visit took place;

- whether any notice, warning, enforcement action, preservation action or
other intervention was considered;

- and whether the Council has retained records explaining why the
demolition was allowed to proceed.

This is particularly important because the building was subsequently
treated within the planning process as an already-cleared site.

4. The 1989 planning application appears to contain a significant
historical discrepancy

The outline planning application submitted by BP Properties Ltd in 1989
states, in the section asking which buildings were to be demolished:

«"None."»

The same application describes the site as "Disused" and the previous use
as "Not known".

This requires explanation because the application followed the demolition
of Great House Farm in December 1988 by approximately one year.

I ask the Council to investigate whether its planning officers:

- were aware of the former Great House Farm building when the 1989
application was processed;

- knew when and how it had been demolished;

- checked the accuracy of the applicant's statement that no buildings were
to be demolished;

- identified the former farmhouse in the planning history and supporting
documentation;

- and considered whether the demolition itself raised any planning,
heritage or enforcement issue requiring investigation.

I am particularly concerned that the planning process appears to have
proceeded on the basis of a cleared site without first establishing the
circumstances in which the historic building had disappeared.

5. Failure to create an adequate record of the lost building

The subsequent archaeological documentation states that the building was
"incompletely understood".

I ask the Council to explain what mitigation, recording or investigation it
required in consequence.

The documentary evidence presently available indicates that substantial
historic fabric and multiple phases of the building existed, yet the
building was destroyed without a complete standing-building survey having
been secured.

I therefore ask the Council to identify:

- all surveys undertaken before demolition;

- all surveys undertaken after demolition;

- all archaeological or architectural advice obtained by the Council;

- all photographs held by the Council;

- all correspondence concerning the building's architectural or historic
importance;

- and the Council's policy or practice in 1988 concerning the recording of
significant unlisted historic buildings at risk.

6. Subsequent planning treatment of the site

Following demolition, the planning process concentrated heavily on
below-ground archaeology, ultimately resulting in archaeological
investigation of the cemetery and associated remains.

I do not suggest that archaeological excavation was inappropriate. My
concern is that the destruction of the standing historic building appears
to have been treated as a fait accompli rather than as an event requiring
accountability and an explanation of how the Council's heritage
responsibilities had been discharged.

The later planning documentation should therefore be reviewed alongside the
records relating to the 1988 demolition.

In particular, I ask the Council to identify precisely when the planning
authority first recorded the former farmhouse as demolished and what
explanation was placed on the planning file for its loss.

7. Matters I ask the Council to investigate

Please investigate and provide a substantive response to the following
questions:

A. What did Vale of Glamorgan Council know about the impending demolition
of Great House Farm before December 1988?

B. What statutory and non-statutory heritage protections were available to
the Council at the time?

C. Were any of those mechanisms considered or discussed?

D. Were any Building Preservation Notice, listing, enforcement, urgent
works, archaeological recording or other protective measures considered?

E. Why was the building apparently destroyed without a comprehensive
standing-building survey?

F. What records does the Council hold concerning the demolition itself?

G. Why did the 1989 planning application proceed despite the recent
demolition of a building identified in the archaeological record as a
"county treasure"?

H. Why was the applicant's answer "None" given to the question concerning
buildings to be demolished, and did the Council investigate the apparent
discrepancy?

I. Did any Council officer consider whether the 1988 demolition constituted
a breach of planning control or otherwise required investigation?

J. Did the Council investigate whether the building had been demolished
lawfully?

K. What heritage assessment was undertaken before the subsequent
development permissions were processed?

L. What lessons has the Council subsequently incorporated into its
procedures for County Treasures and other locally significant historic
buildings?

8. Records requested as part of the investigation

Please preserve and review all relevant records, including planning files,
enforcement records, heritage files, committee papers, officer reports,
internal correspondence, site inspection notes, photographs, archaeological
correspondence and consultation records concerning:

- Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr / Cedfin / Cydfin;

- SMR/HER reference 2038s / GGAT02038s;

- the December 1988 demolition;

- the 1989 outline planning application;

- the 1990 archaeological assessment;

- and the subsequent reserved matters/development applications.

I would also ask that the Council identify any material which has been
destroyed or cannot now be located, together with the applicable
retention/disposal record where one exists.

9. Outcome sought

I am seeking a formal investigation and a reasoned written explanation of
the Council's actions and omissions.

In particular, I ask the Council to determine:

1. Whether its officers discharged the heritage and planning
responsibilities applicable at the time.

2. Whether any failure occurred in relation to the identification,
protection, recording or investigation of Great House Farm.

3. Whether the Council's handling of the 1989 planning application
appropriately addressed the recent demolition of the building.

4. Whether any relevant records have been lost or destroyed and, if so,
when and under what retention arrangements.

5. What procedural lessons arise from the case.

I also request disclosure of the relevant non-exempt records identified
during the complaint investigation, where these are not otherwise
available. I recognise that requests for specific recorded information may
need to be dealt with separately under the appropriate information-access
regime.

I have only recently been able to examine and correlate the surviving
planning, archaeological and heritage documentation sufficiently to
identify these issues. I therefore ask that the Council accepts the
complaint for investigation notwithstanding the age of the events concerned.

Please acknowledge receipt and confirm the complaint reference and the
officer responsible for its investigation.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler of Great House Farm, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, particularly the

subsequent planning process.

thread_title: N610CGV — surviving first-registration records: letter of 30 July 2026 and unanswered follow-ups
subject: Further to Your Enquiry: Ref: 260917-6714794 Title No: WA231076
body:
Enquiry Reference: 260917-6714794 Title Number: WA231076

Dear Customer

I am sorry that the wrong contact information was shown on our letter to you. We are directing our customers to contact us via our contact form<https://www.gov.uk/guidance/contact-hm-land-registry#online>.

Background:

HM Land Registry has created many email addresses over the years. We can no longer service the incoming emails or route such emails into our current system.

Planned system improvements:

We plan to remove all reference to individual HM Land Registry email addresses. This process was more complex than expected and some templates still need updating.

Working with our Customers:

We want to ensure that correspondence goes direct to our customer service team. To do this, we now ask customers to use our online contact form. This is why we put an auto-response in place.

Yours faithfully

Laura Cotton
HM Land Registry

We only provide factual information and impartial advice about our procedures. Read more about the advice we give.<https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/hm-land-registry-service-standards/our-service-standards>

Easy and free support to help you work with HM Land Registry:
Guidance for members of the public - GOV.UK<https://www.gov.uk/guidance/guidance-for-members-of-the-public>
Guidance for property professionals - GOV.UK<https://www.gov.uk/guidance/guidance-for-property-professionals>

HM Land Registry's purpose is to protect your land ownership and provide services and data that underpin an efficient and informed property market. Our vision is: "A world-leading property market as part of a thriving economy and a sustainable future".

We check all mail and attachments for known viruses. However, you are advised that you open any attachments at your own risk. If you have received this email and it was not intended for you, please let us know, then delete it.

We welcome correspondence in English and Welsh.

To see how HM Land Registry treats your personal information, read our Personal information charter: www.gov.uk/government/organisations/land-registry/about/personal-information-charter.

thread_title: Cadw — Formal complaint of 17 September 2026, re-service and supplement
subject: Great House Farm, Llandough
note: Delivery to cadw@gov.wales was blocked (550 5.4.1) and cadw@wales.gsi.gov.uk failed (domain not found). Copies to cadwplanning@gov.wales and cadw@tfw.wales were delivered.
body:
Mr Wigley,

I am writing to make a *formal complaint to Cadw* concerning the handling and substantive response to my correspondence regarding Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough, and particularly Cadw's 1988 consideration of whether the building should be protected by listing.

I am making this complaint directly to Cadw at this stage because I consider that Cadw should be given a proper opportunity to review and address the matters before any escalation to the wider Welsh Government complaints process.

For the avoidance of doubt, I am *not making a further Freedom of Information request* and I am not simply asking Cadw to produce records which it has already said no longer exist. I accept that Cadw has stated that all records it currently holds concerning the 1988 listing decision have been released.

My complaint concerns what can properly be established from the surviving evidence, whether the responses I have received have adequately addressed that evidence, and whether the historical record can now be described accurately where the underlying file has been lost.
1. The newly identified 1982 evidence

I have now identified a 1 October 1982 consultation letter from the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust concerning the East Vale Local Plan and the proposed Ty Maw Farm site, identified as *H2.1*.

The letter states:

“Ty Maw Farm (H2.1) is designated as a three-acre residential site. As you will see from the enclosed information the settlement at Llandough developed considerably from farming and fishing... Recent excavations at Llandough by the Trust revealed early occupation, part of the villa and medieval grange buildings. There remains a possibility that occupation continues to the north of the church; provision should be made, therefore, for thorough investigative work prior to the development.”

I do not suggest that this document, by itself, establishes that the standing farmhouse was required to be listed.

Its significance is narrower and more demonstrable: *six years before the 1988 demolition, the archaeological and planning system already contained site-specific information identifying Ty Maw Farm as a proposed development site and recording substantial archaeological sensitivity in the immediate Llandough area, including possible continued occupation north of the church.*

That materially affects the historical context in which Cadw's 1988 assessment needs to be understood.

I therefore ask Cadw to address:

   1.

   Whether this 1982 information was held by, available to, or capable of being obtained by Cadw in the period leading to the 1988 decision. 2.

   Whether Cadw has any surviving evidence showing what archaeological, planning or historic-building information was available to the inspectors or decision-makers in 1988. 3.

   Whether there was communication between Cadw and the relevant planning/archaeological authorities concerning the proposed development of Ty Maw Farm and the need for investigation or protection. 4.

   If it is no longer possible to establish whether this evidence was actually considered, whether Cadw will expressly acknowledge that uncertainty rather than treating the absence of the historic file as evidence that the relevant information was absent.

2. The 1974 RCAHMW survey

I have previously drawn Cadw's attention to the 26 April 1974 Royal Commission survey by H.J. Thomas at ST16817331.

That survey recorded Great House Farm as a historic building, including features such as the late seventeenth-century character of the house, its cross-passage arrangement, adze-worked beams, ogee stops and barrel-vaulted cellar.

Cadw has stated that only two photographs from its relevant historic material survive and that it cannot now establish whether the 1974 survey was taken into account in the 1988 listing consideration.

I accept that this may now be incapable of being proved from the surviving file.

However, there is an important distinction between:

*“Cadw cannot now establish whether the information was considered”*

and

*“there is no evidence that the information was available or relevant.”*

The surviving RCAHMW material demonstrates that professional historic-building recording existed well before the 1988 decision.

I therefore ask Cadw to address specifically whether that material was available to Cadw through the inter-agency heritage system at the time and, if so, what can now be established about its availability.
3. Cadw's own evidence that listing was actively being considered in 1988

The surviving contemporary material indicates that in December 1988 Cadw was actively considering emergency protection/spot-listing of Great House Farm, including inspection and consultation concerning the building's historic significance.

That is important because it demonstrates that this was not retrospectively invented as a heritage issue decades later. Cadw itself was considering protection immediately before the building was demolished.

Cadw's present position is that the historical listing file no longer survives and that its retention arrangements at the time cannot now be established with certainty.

I am not asking Cadw to speculate about what a destroyed file contained.

I am asking Cadw to distinguish clearly between:

   - what the surviving evidence positively establishes;
   - what information was demonstrably available by 1988;
   - what actions by Cadw in 1988 can still be established;
   - what cannot now be established because the historic record has been lost; and
   - any conclusions Cadw considers cannot responsibly be drawn.

That distinction is particularly important when assessing whether the surviving record provides a sufficiently reliable account of what happened.
4. The planning authority and temporary protection

I also wish to clarify the position concerning temporary protection.

I am not suggesting that Cadw itself necessarily possessed the statutory power to serve a Building Preservation Notice. I understand that such protection was a matter for the relevant local planning authority under the legislation then in force.

The question for Cadw is therefore whether, during the 1988 consideration, *Cadw advised, discussed or communicated with the relevant planning authority concerning any available temporary protection mechanism or the need to prevent demolition pending consideration of listing.*

If Cadw cannot establish what was discussed because the records no longer survive, that should be stated expressly.
5. The later description of Great House Farm as “a listed building”

I have also identified later archaeological/planning documentation in which the former site is described in terms including:

“The site formerly contained Great House Farm (a listed building).”

I am not asserting that this wording conclusively proves that Great House Farm was formally listed at that time.

I am asking Cadw to explain, insofar as the surviving evidence permits, whether there is any known provenance for that description and whether Cadw considers it accurate, erroneous, or simply impossible now to determine.

This is relevant because it illustrates the existence of potentially conflicting historical accounts concerning the building's protection status.
6. The significance of the loss of the 1988 record

Cadw has understandably stated that the historic file cannot now be produced.

However, the loss of that file creates a historical evidential limitation; it should not automatically resolve questions arising from the surviving evidence in Cadw's favour.

The appropriate conclusion may simply be that some aspects of the 1988 decision *cannot now be reconstructed with certainty*.

I would therefore like Cadw to consider whether its previous responses have drawn that distinction sufficiently clearly.
7. What I am asking Cadw to do

I am asking Cadw to treat this as a formal complaint and provide a substantive response addressing the following:

*A.* Whether the newly identified 1982 GGAT evidence materially changes Cadw's understanding of the information environment surrounding Ty Maw Farm before the 1988 demolition.

*B.* Whether Cadw can establish that the 1974 RCAHMW survey was available to it in 1988.

*C.* Whether Cadw can establish what archaeological, planning and historic-building information was available to its officers when the building was being considered for protection.

*D.* What can now be established about Cadw's communications with the local planning authority and other heritage bodies during the 1988 listing consideration.

*E.* Whether temporary protection was discussed or advised upon and, if not capable of being established, whether Cadw will state that plainly.

*F.* What can be established about the inspection of Great House Farm and the ultimate listing decision.

*G.* Whether Cadw accepts that the loss of the historic file means that some aspects of the 1988 decision can no longer be reconstructed reliably.

*H.* Whether Cadw considers the surviving documentary evidence, including the 1974 survey and 1982 archaeological/planning evidence, should be reflected in any relevant contemporary heritage record or historical account.

*I.* Whether Cadw can explain the provenance, insofar as it is capable of doing so, of the later description of the former site as containing “a listed building.”

*J.* Whether Cadw considers that its previous responses have adequately distinguished between the absence of surviving evidence and evidence that something did not happen.
8. Scope of this complaint

I want to be clear that I am not asking Cadw to determine my family's wider property or title claims, nor am I asking Cadw to reach a predetermined conclusion about the historical ownership of the land.

Those matters are separate.

This complaint is confined to *Cadw's own heritage-related role, the 1988 protection/listing process, the information that can now be established as having existed, and the adequacy and accuracy of Cadw's present explanation of that history.*

I am also not asking Cadw to speculate about missing documents. On the contrary, I ask that the absence of those documents be treated as an evidential limitation and expressly identified as such.
9. Requested outcome

I would like Cadw to:

   1.

   Register this as a formal complaint and provide a complaint reference. 2.

   Have the matter reviewed by an appropriate person who has not simply repeated the previous FOI position. 3.

   Provide a point-by-point response to the matters above, taking account of the newly identified 1982 evidence. 4.

   Correct or clarify any part of Cadw's previous correspondence that is found to have been incomplete, inaccurate or insufficiently qualified. 5.

   State clearly which matters can now be established, which cannot, and which remain uncertain because the historical records no longer survive.

I regard that as a proportionate and reasonable opportunity for Cadw to address the matter directly before I consider whether escalation through the Welsh Government complaints process is necessary.

Yours sincerely,

*Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)*
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: FOI/EIR 00211483 — 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES consultation, conditions and reserved matters
subject: Great House Farm, Llandough (89/01396/OUT)
body:
Dear FOI Unit,

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and/or the Environmental
Information Regulations 2004 (whichever regime the Council considers
applicable to the material), I am requesting information held in relation
to:

- Planning application *89/01396/OUT* (outline permission granted 13
March 1990); and
- The subsequent reserved matters application *92/00671/RES*,

both concerning land at Great House Farm, Leckwith Road, Llandough,
subsequently developed as Church View Close.

I am seeking to reconstruct the documentary planning and consultation
record between the outline permission and the subsequent
detailed/reserved-matters approval.
1. Consultation responses to application 89/01396/OUT

The Council's own case officer's report on application 89/01396/OUT
records, in its consultations section:

"Cardiff Bay Development Corporation: No objections – however, the
Corporation would hope that the trees on the slope of the site facing
north-west are retained and that the public right of way which runs through
the site will be retained."

The same report refers to further consultation responses from the *National
Rivers Authority* and the *County Engineer* by reference to attached typed
sheets ("please type attached sh②" and "please type attached sh③"), without
reproducing their substantive contents in the disclosed copy.

Please therefore provide:

1. The *complete original written response from the Cardiff Bay Development
Corporation* concerning application 89/01396/OUT, including any
accompanying letter, report, plan, attachment or other document forming
part of that consultation response.

2. The *complete National Rivers Authority consultation response* referred
to in the report as one of the attached sheets, including the original
document and any accompanying material.

3. The *complete County Engineer consultation response* referred to in the
report as one of the attached sheets, including the original document and
any accompanying material.

I am deliberately not relying upon the handwritten numbering of sheets ②
and ③ to identify which sheet belongs to which consultee, as the numerals
are difficult to distinguish in the surviving copy. Please identify the
corresponding sheet/document by reference to its contents or file
provenance.

4. Any *covering correspondence, transmission record or internal record*
showing when the NRA and County Engineer responses were received by the
Council and how those responses were placed on, incorporated into or
considered as part of the planning file.

2. Archaeological assessment and discharge of outline conditions

Please provide:

5. The *formal decision notice and complete schedule of conditions* issued
in connection with planning application 89/01396/OUT, including any
condition concerning archaeological investigation, evaluation, assessment,
excavation, recording, preservation or protection.

6. All records held by the Council demonstrating the *discharge,
implementation or consideration of any archaeological condition*
attached to the 1990 outline permission, including any archaeological
evaluation, field assessment, report, correspondence, approval, discharge
notice, consultation response or internal officer record.

7. Any correspondence or documentation showing how the Council considered
the findings of that archaeological work in determining the subsequent
reserved matters application 92/00671/RES.

3. Reserved matters application 92/00671/RES

Please provide:

8. The *formal decision notice* for application 92/00671/RES, including the
complete schedule of any conditions attached to the approval.

9. The consultation responses and representations received in connection
with 92/00671/RES, including any response or representation from
the *Cardiff
Bay Development Corporation*, if one exists.

10. Any officer report, committee report, delegated report, recommendation
or internal planning assessment relating to the determination of
92/00671/RES.

11. Any document recording the Council's consideration of the relationship
between the reserved-matters proposal and the parameters established by the
outline permission 89/01396/OUT.

4. Change from the outline scheme to the reserved-matters scheme

The officer's report for the outline application describes the indicative
scheme as *18 dwellings*, whereas the subsequent reserved-matters scheme
appears to comprise *20 dwellings*.

Please therefore provide:

12. Any document held by the Council recording or explaining the change from
the indicative *18-dwelling* scheme at outline stage to the *20-dwelling*
scheme submitted/approved at reserved-matters stage.

13. Any planning assessment, officer report, correspondence,
committee/delegated report or other record explaining the planning basis
upon which the additional two dwellings were considered acceptable under
the outline permission.

14. Any document identifying the relevant condition, parameter, planning
provision or other mechanism under application 89/01396/OUT under which the
reserved-matters scheme was considered capable of differing from the
indicative 18-dwelling layout.

5. Scope and record availability

For the avoidance of doubt, this is *not a request for a general search of
all historic records concerning Great House Farm*. It is specifically
directed to the planning records and decision-making documents identified
above for applications *89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES*.

Please search the relevant planning application files and associated
archived/scanned material, including attachments and documents stored
separately from the principal application file where those documents form
part of the application or consultation record.

Please supply the information electronically, such as scanned copies, where
practicable.

If any requested record is *not held*, please confirm this specifically for
the relevant item rather than leaving the point unanswered.

If the Council considers that any information is exempt from disclosure,
please identify the *specific exemption or exception relied upon* and
explain its application.

If any of the identified historical records were previously held but are no
longer available, please confirm, where recorded:

- whether the record was destroyed, transferred, archived elsewhere or
otherwise disposed of;
- the date or approximate date of that action, if recorded;
- the authority or process under which it occurred; and
- whether any surviving catalogue, disposal schedule, transfer record or
other audit trail exists.

I also understand that the application for housing began much further back
as a petition was made in 1974 for 13 houses. Please could you give me a
reference or link or that entire planning application record too.

Please acknowledge receipt of this request and provide a reference number.

I understand that the statutory response period is 20 working days.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: N610CGV — surviving first-registration records: letter of 30 July 2026 and unanswered follow-ups
subject: N610CGV — WA231076 / WA240304
body:
Haste,

This supplements my emails of 16 September 2026 (points 1–14) on N610CGV / WA231076 and WA240304. It is not a complaint, not a request to reopen the stage 2 review of 25 May 2026, and not a FOIA request.
I have not previously asked HM Land Registry to record the following construction of the title chain. I do so now as a factual statement of the case I put on the instruments and their plans. I am not asking you to determine ownership. I am asking you to confirm what the surviving first-registration records show about which parcel was lodged. The land I refer to as the House Plot is the former farmhouse, garden and curtilage of Great House Farm, Llandough, immediately west / north-west of St Dochdwy’s Church, later part of Church View Close, CF64 2NN. My case on the chain is:
The holding was two parcels. The 1916 Bute agricultural tenancy (John Williams) covered both. Farm rents and cottage rents were accounted separately on the Bute rental listings.
After quarrying ceased in or about 1928, the House Plot was treated as severed from the agricultural tenancy and held as a separate proprietary parcel by those through whom I claim.
The 1938 conveyance from the Bute interest to Western Ground Rents Limited, construed against its plan, conveyed the eastern agricultural parcel. It did not convey the House Plot.
The May 1939 agricultural tenancy between WGR and John Williams concerned that eastern parcel. It did not comprise the House Plot.
The 1955 enforcement papers and the 11 December 1962 Cardiff County Court possession order against Frederick Buckler and Mary Williams (sued as Mrs Buckler) were directed at the farmhouse and garden. Those proceedings asserted a right to possession. They did not construe the 1877, 1938 or later deeds and were not a conveyance of the House Plot into the WGR estate. The 31 December 1969 conveyance (WGR to the BP Pension Trust parties), the 23 May 1975 conveyance (BP Pension Trust Limited to BP Properties Limited), and the 1982 first registration of WA231076 could only pass such land as then stood in that documentary estate. On the construction above, that estate did not include the House Plot.
Title WA231076 (and WA240304, later amalgamated) nevertheless included the House Plot. That is the alleged mistake as to extent.
Please therefore add these numbered questions to the live enquiry (also customer-support refs 260812-6561894, 260812-6565153, 260917-6714794, 260917-6714796 and 260917-6718215):
Confirm whether any surviving first-registration document for WA231076 or WA240304 identifies, by plan, OS parcel, colouring, exception, reservation or recital, a distinction between (a) the farmhouse, garden and curtilage and (b) the eastern agricultural / quarrying parcel.
Confirm whether the 1938 Bute–WGR conveyance and plan, or the 1939 tenancy and plan, were lodged on either first-registration file. If held, give title and item number. If only recited, say so. If neither lodged nor recited, say so.
Confirm whether the 23 May 1975 conveyance and plan (WA240304 items 11 and 12 on your 30 July 2026 schedule) describe or colour the House Plot as included, excluded, excepted or reserved. If you will not read the deed, identify it as an OC2 item and say so.
Confirm whether the 31 December 1969 WGR conveyance (point 10 of my 16 September email) describes or colours the House Plot as included. Same options as 17.
Confirm whether any examiner note, requisition or Linklaters & Paines letter on the surviving files addresses the geographic extent of the land applied for, as distinct from the applicant’s paper title generally. I do not ask you to accept this construction. I ask you to say what the listed records contain about parcel identity, or to state in writing that you will not examine them and that the questions should be answered by Form OC2.
Yours sincerely,
Sion Buckler
N610CGV — WA231076 / WA240304

thread_title: Escalation to the Leader — ward member silence and the commemorative tree (Monitoring Officer reply)
from: Victoria Davidson, Monitoring Officer/Head of Legal and Democratic Services (VDavidson@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk)
subject: RE: Escalation — Llandough ward member silence: Great House Farm / Church View Close and removal of commemorative tree
body:
Dear Mr Buckler
Thank you for your recent correspondence which I am responding to on behalf of the Leader, concerning Great House Farm/Church View Close, the removal of a commemorative tree and your communications with Councillor Carroll.
I have considered the matters you have raised.
As you are aware, I have previously responded to your concerns regarding Councillor Carroll's lack of response to your correspondence. Having reviewed those concerns, I concluded that the matter did not fall within the Council's Corporate Complaints Policy and I did not identify any basis for further action under the Members' Code of Conduct process. The Council has no mechanism by which it can compel an elected member to respond to correspondence from a constituent and, accordingly, the Council's consideration of that aspect of the matter is concluded.
Please note that the Leader is not responsible for the conduct of Members other than those with her own political group
I note that your recent correspondence extends beyond the issue of Councillor Carroll's responsiveness and raises a broader range of concerns relating to historical land ownership, planning and heritage matters associated with Great House Farm/Church View Close, together with a request for information regarding the removal of a commemorative tree.
In relation to the tree, I am making enquiries to establish whether the Council holds any records which may assist in answering your question regarding its removal. This is being dealt with by the Information Governance Team, I have copied in the FOI unit email domain. If relevant information is held by the Council, I will advise you accordingly. Equally, if no such records are held, I will confirm that position.
In respect of the wider matters raised in your correspondence, it is important that I clarify the scope of the Council's role. The Council is not able to determine disputed ownership of land, revisit historical legal proceedings, adjudicate upon competing title claims, or investigate allegations of fraud or other criminal conduct. Those matters fall within the jurisdiction of the courts, HM Land Registry, the police and other external bodies as appropriate.
Whilst I appreciate the strength of feeling reflected in your correspondence and recognise the significance that these matters have for you and your family, the Council must limit its involvement to those issues which fall within its statutory functions and responsibilities. Any response provided by the Council will therefore be confined to matters upon which it may properly comment and any information which it may hold.
The FOI team will write to you further once enquiries regarding the tree have been completed.
Yours sincerely,

But I am bona fide. I left my military career with full honours.

In any case, separately from the Councillor Carroll complaint which you
closed today. This complaint concerns two connected matters: the custody
and handling of Llandough Community Council records concerning Great House
Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, and the completeness and treatment of Vale of
Glamorgan Council's planning and heritage records relating to application
89/01396/OUT and the subsequent reserved-matters application.

I appreciate that you do not employ the former Clerk, Mr Paul R. Egan. I am
nevertheless raising the matter with you as Monitoring Officer because the
underlying planning file is a Vale file, the Community Council's records
form part of the local documentary record, and I need a clear written
account of who now has responsibility for those records and what has
happened to them.

Everyone's also got a boss. Mine being God and my 56 British Soldier
shareholders in my US based company private security group. So feel free to
pass this up your ranks to your overlords if you can't or won't make sense
of it or take any action.

I also want to be precise about what I am, and am not, alleging. I do not
have evidence that Mr Egan removed, altered or destroyed any document. Nor
can I establish from the present evidence why he retired when he did. The
fact that a long-serving Clerk retired during the period in which I was
seeking these records is, however, a material chronology, particularly
because he had initially adopted a position of not engaging beyond a
statutory search. I therefore ask the Council to establish the facts rather
than assume either that the matter is innocuous or that any wrongdoing
occurred.

   1. Llandough Community Council records

In May and June 2026 I asked Mr Egan for Community Council records
concerning Great House Farm, including material concerning the events
surrounding my late father's involvement with the property in 1988.

On 14 June 2026 Mr Egan stated that minute books from 1982 onwards had been
deposited with Glamorgan Archives in 2002 and relied on section 21 FOIA. He
subsequently retired. On the day of his retirement he directed me towards
Leckwith records and the 1939 Western Ground Rents tenancy with my
great-grandfather.

That tenancy is significant because, on the documents I have examined, it
appears to concern the eastern field rather than the House Plot containing
the farmhouse and associated buildings. I therefore do not regard that
reference as resolving the documentary position concerning Great House Farm
itself.

I need the Council to establish:

   - who is now Clerk and Proper Officer of Llandough Community Council;
   - who currently has custody of its historic minute books, correspondence
   and other records;
   - what records were handed over or inventoried when Mr Egan retired;
   - whether any search has been made specifically for Great House Farm /
   Tŷ Mawr records, rather than relying solely on the general statement that
   minute books were deposited in 2002; and
   - whether any Community Council correspondence, consultation response or
   minute relating to 89/01396/OUT or the later reserved matters survives.

If any part of this falls solely within the responsibility of Llandough
Community Council or the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales, please
identify the appropriate authority and the person to whom I should address
that part of the complaint.

   2. What the existing evidence establishes

This section turns from Community Council custody to the Vale's own
planning and archaeological file for 89/01396/OUT. The points below are
based on documents already in my possession and published archaeological
material, and are separate from the matters in Section 1, where I am asking
the Council to search its records.

   1.

   Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr is recorded in the historic environment
   record as County Treasure, reference SMR/HER 2038s / GGAT02038s, at
   approximately ST 1681 7331. The 1990 GGAT assessment records that, because
   of an ownership dispute and the subsequent sudden destruction of the
   property in 1988, the building was incompletely understood.
   2.

   Outline planning application 89/01396/OUT, submitted by BP Properties
   Ltd, followed the 1988 demolition by approximately a year. The application
   answers the relevant questions as follows: buildings to be demolished —
   "None"; site — "Disused"; previous use — "Not known".
   3.

   The Vale officer material in my possession refers to an outline-stage
   indicative scheme of 18 dwellings. The subsequent reserved-matters scheme
   approved on 3 September 1992 is for 20 dwellings.
   4.

   The 1990 evaluation recorded archaeological potential to the north of
   the churchyard and identified a medium-to-high potential area. What it does
   not establish by itself is the full extent of the archaeological remains
   subsequently encountered.
   5.

   Cotswold Archaeology excavated at the same general location in 1994,
   immediately adjacent to St Dochdwy's Church. The published archaeological
   account records 1,026 burials from an excavated area of 0.22 hectares. I am
   relying on the excavators' published figure rather than the lower secondary
   figure of 858, which appears to conflate different phases of investigation.
   6.

   PPG16 was issued in November 1990 and therefore post-dates the March
   1990 outline decision, but was applicable by the time of the September 1992
   reserved-matters decision. I am not presently asserting what archaeological
   conditions were imposed in 1992. The drawings I hold are stamped as
   approved on 3 September 1992, subject to compliance with conditions if any,
   but I do not hold the decision notice setting out the actual conditions.
   That decision notice is therefore a critical missing document.
   7.

   I am also not treating the handwritten numbering on the surviving
   consultation material as conclusively establishing which sheet relates to
   which responding body. The underlying consultation responses remain
   relevant and should be located irrespective of that numbering issue.
   8.

   The documentary gap that now needs explaining

The sequence is straightforward.

The historic farmhouse and associated buildings were demolished in December
1988.

The subsequent 1989 outline application described the site as "Disused",
stated that there were "None" buildings to be demolished, and gave the
previous use as "Not known".

The 1990 archaeological evaluation had already identified significant
archaeological potential near the churchyard.

The 1992 reserved-matters approval provided for 20 dwellings.

The 1994 excavation subsequently recorded 1,026 burials from 0.22 hectares
immediately adjacent to the church.

What I cannot establish from the records presently available to me is how
the archaeological excavation area relates spatially to the approved
housing layout and retained areas. In particular, I need the 1994
excavation plan and the corresponding Ideal Homes layout so that the two
can be compared accurately.

I also need to understand how the 1989 application descriptions came to be
accepted against the documentary and historic-environment information
already available concerning the demolished farmhouse.

I am not asking the Council to adopt my interpretation of these matters. I
am asking it to establish what was known, what was checked, what was
recorded, and what records still exist.

   4. Specific information and records requested

Please provide a substantive written response to each of the following:

   1.

   Who is currently Clerk and Proper Officer of Llandough Community
   Council, and who has custody of its historic records?
   2.

   Was Llandough Community Council consulted on application 89/01396/OUT
   and/or the subsequent reserved-matters application? If so, please provide
   the consultation requests, replies, minutes and associated correspondence,
   or confirm specifically that no such material is held.
   3.

   Please provide the full planning decision notice dated 3 September 1992,
   including all conditions, rather than the approved drawings alone.
   4.

   Please confirm whether Vale holds the 1994 Cotswold Archaeology
   site/excavation plans and the relevant Ideal Homes development layout
   plans. Please also confirm whether the Council has ever undertaken or
   commissioned a plan-to-plan comparison showing the excavation area against
   the approved development footprint.
   5.

   Please identify the officer or officers responsible for assessing the
   1989 application against the information then available concerning the 1988
   demolition and HER/SMR record 2038s, including the entries "None",
   "Disused" and "Not known".
   6.

   Please confirm what planning, enforcement, conservation/heritage,
   archaeological, consultation, photographic and correspondence records
   remain for the site and where they are presently held.
   7.

   Given the issues raised by my FOI/EIR correspondence and the corporate
   complaint of 17 September 2026, please ensure that surviving records
   concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, including Community Council records
   where they remain identifiable, are preserved pending resolution of these
   matters. I am particularly concerned that records should not disappear
   simply because responsibility has passed from one office-holder to another.
   8.

   Please confirm whether there was a formal handover, inventory or records
   transfer when Mr Egan retired, and whether any such documentation records
   the location of material concerning Great House Farm, planning
   consultations, or the 1988 demolition.
   9.

   Finally, if the Council considers that any aspect concerning Mr Egan's
   conduct as Community Council Clerk falls outside the Vale's jurisdiction,
   please identify the proper route and responsible body rather than simply
   closing that part of the complaint.

I am deliberately separating evidence from inference. I am not alleging
that Mr Egan's retirement was caused by my FOI requests, nor am I alleging
that any individual deliberately concealed records. The timing, however, is
sufficiently relevant that the Council should establish what happened to
the records at the point responsibility changed. The immediate issue is
capable of being answered objectively: what records exist, what was known
to the authority, what checks were carried out, what decisions were made,
and where the missing documents are now.

Please treat this as a formal request for a written governance/records
response and address each numbered question individually. It should be read
alongside FOI/EIR reference 00210772 and my correspondence of 17–18
September 2026.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
------------------------------

Changes made: added the Re: line, opened Section 2 with a sentence flagging
the shift from Community Council custody to the Vale's own file, and merged
the two closing paragraphs to drop the repeated point. Everything else —
including all the evidence/inference hedging — is untouched. Want it as a
Word doc or PDF instead, or any further tweaks?

thread_title: Sept 2026 EIR request — HER source file GGAT02038s (c.1880 ironwork)
subject: Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff
note: Sent as a new Gmail thread but continues the 8 September request; Heneb's reply of 6 October refers to it.
body:
Dear Calli,

Further to my email of 8 September 2026 concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, I attach a formal schedule of the records I am seeking, so that the request is easier for Heneb to work through and to allocate internally. I have also completed your online enquiry form, so the request is in your preferred channel.

I appreciate a response would not fall due until 6 October, so this is not a chaser. It is to put the detail in one place and to clarify the basis of the request.

On your note of 22 May. You are right that Heneb, as a limited company, is not a public authority under the Freedom of Information Act 2000, and I do not pursue that. Two separate points remain, and I would welcome Heneb's position on each.

First, the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 apply on a different test — regulation 2(2) reaches bodies carrying out functions of public administration relating to the environment, or under the control of a public authority. If Heneb considers it falls outside that, please say so expressly with brief reasons, so that I can direct the request elsewhere.

Second, and independently, the Historic Environment Record is a statutory record: sections 194 and 195 of the Historic Environment (Wales) Act 2023 require the Welsh Ministers to maintain an HER for every local authority area and to make it available for public inspection, and Heneb keeps the south-east Wales record on their behalf. I therefore ask in the alternative that this be treated as a request for access under that regime and under Heneb's own policy.

Two things that will make this easier. If any item is too broad, please tell me which and I will narrow it rather than have the whole request refused. And if Heneb can supply, as a first step, simply a schedule or index of the records it holds for this site — without copying them — that would let me target the rest precisely and save your staff considerable time. I am content to inspect material by appointment at Baglan or at the HER, and any reasonable copying or staff-time charge can be notified to me in advance for approval.

Two small administrative points. Please confirm which legal entity now holds the records and functions formerly of Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd, and who within Heneb handles access requests of this kind.

Finally, since my correspondence in May was framed more formally: my purpose is documentary. I am reconstructing the record of a farm my family occupied for generations, and I would far rather do that with Heneb's help than around it.

I should say plainly that I have read GGAT's December 1993 notification to the Vale of Glamorgan that Condition 18 had not been complied with, and the recommendation that a Breach of Condition Notice be issued. Whatever else is in dispute about this site, that was the Trust doing its job properly, and I am grateful for it.

Thank you in advance for your time in this matter,

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: Cadw — Formal complaint of 17 September 2026, re-service and supplement
subject: Formal complaint of 17 September 2026 — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — non-delivery and re-service
body:
Wigley,

I sent you the formal complaint below on 17 September 2026. I have since established that it never reached you.

It was addressed to cadw@gov.wales, which rejected it — my mail server recorded "message blocked… the address couldn't be found or is unable to receive email." A copy addressed to cadw@wales.gsi.gov.uk also failed, that domain having been decommissioned. The only addresses that accepted it were cadwplanning@gov.wales and cadw@tfw.wales.

The latter is Cadw's visitor-services contact centre operated by Transport for Wales, which replied on 18 September under reference #628635887 to say it had been passed to their complaints manager. That is plainly not the right destination for a complaint about a 1988 listing assessment, and I do not want it pursued there. I would be grateful if that reference could be closed. I should add that cadw@gov.wales has now rejected correspondence from me on three separate occasions — 23 January, 29 August and 17 September 2026. If that address is still published anywhere as a contact point for Cadw, it may be worth someone looking at.

I am therefore re-serving the complaint on you directly, unchanged. The text below is exactly as sent on 17 September. Please treat it as received today, and please let me have a complaint reference.

Two points of clarification, so that nothing is misread.

First, this is not a further Freedom of Information request. I accept your email of 4 September, in which you confirmed that Cadw has released all the records it holds concerning the 1988 listing decision, and I am not asking you to produce documents you have already said no longer survive. I am conscious that I have made requests to Cadw and to the Welsh Government Information Rights Unit since May of this year and that they have been answered. My complaint is not that records are being withheld. It is about what can properly be established from the evidence that does survive, and about whether Cadw's account distinguishes clearly enough between "we cannot now establish this" and "this did not happen."

Second, I am treating this as stage one of the Welsh Government complaints process, not stage two. You directed me to that process on 4 September. I have copied the Complaints Advice Team so that the complaint is logged and dated, but I am not asking for a formal investigation yet. I would rather Cadw had the first opportunity to answer it. I will only escalate if the stage one response does not engage with the ten matters set out at section 7 below.

One further matter, which I raise in the hope it is useful rather than as part of the complaint. Cadw's 1988 file is lost, but Cadw did not correspond with itself. Any letters Cadw wrote in 1988 about this building were received by the Royal Commission, by Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council, and by the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust, and copies may survive in their files even though yours have gone. I have requests with the Royal Commission and with Heneb which cover exactly that. If either produces Cadw correspondence you no longer hold, I will send it to you, as I said I would in August. I would rather Cadw's own record of this was complete than score a point off its being incomplete.

I look forward to a complaint reference and to a substantive reply.

Yours sincerely,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: FOI/EIR 00211463 — planning appendices C, D, E and Policy H.2 (89/01396/OUT)
subject: Re: FOI/EIR request - Case Ref/ 00211463 — clarification and refinement of request
body:
Freedom of Information Officer,

Case Ref: 00211463 — request received 17 September 2026

I write to clarify and refine the above request while it remains open,
having now examined the original manuscript of the planning officer's
report rather than a transcription. My earlier request named two
organisations; the document in fact identifies the correspondents
differently, and I ask that the request be read as follows.

The passage relied upon
The planning officer's report on application 89/01396/OUT (residential
development including new access road, land at Great House Farm, Leckwith
Road, Llandough, Penarth; outline permission granted 13 March 1990) states,
at page 2:

"Two letters have been received from the Barry Preservation Society and
Civic Trust and a local County Councillor (who is a member of the Glamorgan
Gwent Archaeological Trust) making representations in respect of this
application and a copy of both these letters are attached to this report as
Appendices 'C' and 'D' respectively."

The following paragraph of the same report states:

"The Applicants' Agents have written in response to the report of the
Glamorgan Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd. on the site and a copy of this
letter is attached to this report as Appendix 'E'."

What I request
Appendix "C" to the officer's report on 89/01396/OUT — the letter from the
Barry Preservation Society and Civic Trust.

Appendix "D" — the letter from the local County Councillor referred to,
together with that Councillor's name.

Appendix "E" — the letter from the Applicants' Agents responding to the
report of the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd.

A list of all appendices ("A" to "E" or further) to that officer's report,
so that the complete annex set is identified.

Any register, index, schedule or file list for application 89/01396/OUT
recording the documents originally held on the file.
A further document referred to in the same report

The officer's report also records, of the East Vale Local Plan:

"The greater part of the land is allocated for new residential development
in the East Vale Local Plan (Policy No. H.2.) The information supporting
the policy states that buildings on the site should be retained, however
were unfortunately demolished a little while ago."

I therefore also request:
The text of Policy H.2 of the East Vale Local Plan and the supporting
information to that policy referred to above, in the version current in
1989–1990.

Points on handling
These are documents the Council's own report states were attached to it. If
any of them is not held, I ask the Council to say so expressly, and to
state (a) when it ceased to be held, (b) under what retention schedule or
disposal decision, and (c) whether any record of that disposal exists. A
response that "no additional information has been identified" would not
address a request for annexes that the Council's own report records as
attached.

I note the Council's letter of 11 September 2026 in a related matter, which
stated that "further historical documentation has been found... not
necessarily Council documentation but is nonetheless in the Council's
possession". I ask that this material be searched in responding to the
present request.

I intend this as a clarification and refinement of case 00211463 under the
Council's duty to advise and assist (s.16 FOIA 2000 / reg. 9 EIR 2004), and
not as a new request. If the Council takes the view that any part of it
must be treated as a fresh request, please confirm that in writing,
identify which parts, and give the revised due date, so that I am not left
uncertain which deadline applies to which element.
I should be grateful for confirmation of receipt.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
