thread_title: Formal complaint — HER identifiers and the 1978–1995 record (investigating officer Steven Foulston)
subject: Formal complaint — GGAT / Heneb: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — HER identifiers and the 1978–1995 record
body:
Chief Executive / Complaints Officer,

This is a formal complaint to Heneb: The Trust for Welsh Archaeology, as operational successor to the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust, and to Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Limited (The), company 01276976, which remains an active company with its registered office at Heneb's address.

It concerns Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan (near Penarth / Cardiff); ST 1681 7331; NPRN 20182. Cadw and RCAHMW have supplied three unreconciled HER references for the same site: GGAT02038s, GGAT03586s and GGATE003872.

This is not a chaser of my records request of 8 September 2026 or the schedule of 19 September (ref GHF/HENEB/2026-09-20). That request remains open and is due a response by 6 October. Please treat this complaint as a separate file and give it a complaint reference.

What this is not. It is not an allegation that GGAT demolished the house, advised that it be demolished, or decided that it should not be listed. It is not an allegation of dishonesty, bad faith or criminal conduct. It is not a title claim and I do not ask you to adjudicate BP v Buckler. GGAT's letters of 13 and 15 December 1993, recommending a Breach of Condition Notice when Condition 18 had not been met, were the Trust doing its curatorial job. That is recorded here so it is not lost in what follows.

The charge, put narrowly. GGAT was the public curator of the regional record; the adviser who told the planning authority it could not determine 89/01396/OUT without an archaeological assessment; the body which, in the same document, specified machine-trench evaluation, quoted £2,000 and two weeks, and recorded that it was already negotiating that work with BP Properties; the contractor who then executed that evaluation on a churchside monastic site its own 1978–80 excavations and its own 1982 letter had already flagged; and the author of a zoning map which treated as empty ground in which, four years later, inhumations were found a few centimetres below the topsoil. Disclosure of the dual role was not management of it. The public record still does not reliably carry what was found. Heneb's entire substantive reply since May is one sentence about corporate form.

I enclose GGAT — Forensic Critique, Version 4.0.0 (21 September 2026). It distinguishes established fact, reasonable inference, what cannot be established, and facts that cut against the criticism. Where earlier versions were wrong, the corrections are printed and kept. The critique is the sourcing. This letter is the complaint. Please answer the letter. Treat the critique as the schedule of sources, not as a substitute for numbered answers.

1. I have not seen the HER

I do not assert the wording of GGAT02038s, because I have not been allowed to read it. Cadw has said the content of the HER is managed by Heneb. RCAHMW and Cadw have given three different identifiers for the same site. Tests of Archwilio on 20 September 2026 did not return an error for unresolved records. They returned a different record, from a different trust, for a different site, with no warning:

GGAT02038s → GAT46242 (Gwynedd desk-based assessment)
GGAT03586s → GAT92911 (farmstead, Warwick Place, Gwynedd)
GGAT02038s, alternative path, three attempts → E001657 each time

A control query for an indexed record returned correctly. Please test those three queries, correct the substitution if confirmed, and tell me the outcome. Then permit inspection of the source file and supply an index of every linked site and event record with its correct reference.

2. "Partially recorded" is RCAHMW's phrase, not a finding I have verified on the HER

On 10 June 2026 Dr Adam Coward quoted NMR 6048945: "The house remained partially recorded because of problems created by an ownership dispute. The house and farm buildings were suddenly and completely destroyed by B. P. Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988 amid considerable local controversy."

That is the Royal Commission's file. I hold H. J. Thomas's measured ground-floor plan of 26 April 1974, at 1:100, identifying the principal rooms including the Dairy and recording the beams. GGAT reproduced that plan as Figure 2 of its 1990 assessment, by kind permission. A measured ground-floor survey that could not reach the first floor and roof is not, without more, a failed survey.

Please state, from records you hold:
(a) whether the HER uses the phrase "partially recorded", and if so from which source;
(b) what parts of the building the 1974 survey measured, and what it did not;
(c) what contemporaneous document, if any beyond NMR 6048945, establishes that access was restricted by the ownership dispute, by whom, on what date, and to whom;
(d) whether Trench 7 of 1990 (north-east corner / former dairy, stone floor, mortared partition) was ever reconciled against the 1974 plan, and if the Trench 7 drawings, photographs and grid survive.

3. What GGAT held in 1988, and what it did not do

On 1 October 1982 GGAT told the Vale that occupation might continue north of the church and that thorough investigative work should precede development. Between that letter and November 1988 no GGAT act concerning this site has been identified. RCAHMW added to its 1974 plan on 12 December 1988, six days after the demolition. There is no equivalent GGAT event. The 1990 report notes architectural features "observed in the rubble" and then begins GGAT's own account with the words "Following the demolition… GGAT entered into discussion with Debenham Tewson".

Please state what the SMR entry contained immediately before December 1988; whether the 1982 advice was on it; whether any emergency building record, watching brief on the demolition or the rubble, or post-demolition fabric report exists; and where the carved stone and other architectural material later referred to now is.

4. "County treasure"

GGAT 1989 §2.3: "At present our information on the Great House Farm area is limited to the records of the recently demolished property which was listed as a 'county treasure'." The phrase conferred no statutory protection. Identify the list or card, the date, the criteria, and what information about the building accompanied it. If you do not hold that document, say so.

5. Specify, price, bid, execute

In one 1989 consultee report GGAT advised that 89/01396/OUT should not be determined without an assessment; specified machine-excavator trial trenching; quoted two weeks at £2,000; and recorded that negotiations with BP Properties via Debenham Tewson were already under way. BP then commissioned GGAT. The 1990 report disclosed a "dual role" and invited either party to go elsewhere. Disclosure is recorded. It is not the same as management.

The IFA Code of approved practice for contractual arrangements was adopted on 17 September 1990, after the assessment was delivered. It does not bind that commission. The Welsh Archaeological Trusts' Code of Practice dates from November 1997 and is not applied retrospectively. What did bind the 1989–90 arrangement, as contemporaneous standards rather than as a pleaded cause of action: the IFA Code of Conduct in force from June 1985; the BADLG Code, which GGAT expressly endorsed in the 1989 report; section 13 of the Supply of Goods and Services Act 1982 as the implied standard of care between GGAT and BP (the family was not a party); and the fiduciary duty of charity trustees to identify and manage conflicts, not merely to notify two commercial counterparties.

On 18 May 1994 GGAT's Curatorial Section wrote, of another contractor: "An archaeological contractor should never be in the position of writing his own Brief as well as carrying out the work." That principle was not met by GGAT's own 1989–90 arrangement.

Please identify who wrote the 1989 recommendation, who accepted the commission, whether those functions were separated, whether trustees or Cadw were told, and who wrote the 1990 brief. If you hold Appendix "B" to the officer's report (GGAT's further comments of 8 February 1990), Appendix "D" (the representation from a County Councillor identified as a member of GGAT), or Appendix "E" (the applicant's agents' written response to GGAT's report), produce them. None of those three is in the planning file released in 2026. Appendix "A" is. I do not assert that GGAT removed them. I ask whether copies survive in GGAT/Heneb files.

6. The 1990 method against GGAT's own model

GGAT had excavated an early-medieval cemetery, a Roman villa and a Tewkesbury Abbey grange immediately south of the same church, on the same alkaline Liassic geology, and had written that occupation might continue north of it. It chose eight machine-cut trenches, some placed "at random", and then rated uninvestigated eastern ground "non existent to low" potential. That rating converted a logistical limit into an empirical claim. Cotswold's December 1994 preliminary report recorded that burials continued into that zone and "lay only a few centimetres below the topsoil".

I do not say a 1990 evaluation had to predict 1,026 burials. I ask whether the method was capable of detecting shallow inhumations on ground where GGAT's own experience predicted excellent bone survival, and whether the 1990 evaluation has ever been reviewed against the 1994 results. If it has not, will Heneb review it now.

7. Human remains and the 1981 Act

GGAT identified the Disused Burial Grounds (Amendment) Act 1981 and found disarticulated human bone by the churchyard wall. That Act turns on whether the land is a burial ground. A colour-coded potential map cannot answer it. What legal advice was obtained, when, and from whom? What evidence set the burial-ground boundary? Was a review undertaken after 1994?

8. Two burial figures, both correct

Cotswold's December 1994 preliminary report, §4.2: 858 inhumations and 152 disarticulated bone groups. Holbrook and Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005): 1,026 burials comprising 814 articulated inhumations and 212 disarticulated bone groups, of which 801 skeletons received full osteological analysis; "by far the largest Early-medieval burial population so far recovered from Wales". They are the same excavation counted twice. Please confirm which figure the HER now carries, and that both stages are identified as such.

9. The c.1880 ironwork sentence, and what Amgueddfa Cymru now holds

GGAT 1990: "it is likely that some medieval ironwork which is held by the National Museum of Wales was discovered under the rear wing c 1880 (RCAHMW 1988)." By 2005 that hedged sentence had become flat assertion in print.

Amgueddfa Cymru's disclosures of 25 August 2026 (FOI 2026-024 and internal review 22 September 2026) and 22 September 2026 (FOI 2026-032) establish the following, so far as the Museum holds recorded information:

(a) No accession, donation, transfer or deposit answering a visor, lance, helmet, armour, soldier, horse, or nineteenth-century discovery under the farmhouse floor.
(b) Accession 82.44H is the 1979 GGAT excavation assemblage. Collected by Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd, 1979; donated 14 June 1982 by Wales & West Housing Association Ltd; bibliographic reference Owen-John
1988. The collections database locality field is "Llandough Roman Villa", NGR ST 168 733 — not "Great House Farm".
(c) Accession 95.56H is the 1994 Cotswold Archaeological Trust cemetery assemblage. Collected by CAT, 1994; donated 28 July 1994 by Ideal Homes Wales Ltd. Locality field: "Great House Farm Llandough", NGR ST 1681 7331. Period on the human-remains entries: Early Medieval (c.400–c.1070).
(d) Accession 63.24 is objects stated to have been found at Church Farm, Llandough, in 1858. The Museum's explanatory note of 22 September 2026 records that this is the only paperwork on that file, and that staff consider it possible those objects are the basis of the later local story. That is the Museum's observation, not a finding I ask you to adopt as fact.

Qualify or withdraw the 1880 sentence if you hold no source beyond the 1990 wording. Carry 82.44H and 95.56H on the principal HER description, with collector, donor, donation date, locality field as catalogued, and NGR. If the HER still points a professional user first to a post-medieval dwelling, that is a record defect against what both excavations produced and what the national museum now catalogues.

Please also confirm whether GGAT retained copies of the 1980 donation correspondence with the National Museum (letters of 14 and 24 April 1980 are on the public record) and of any transfer file for 82.44H.

10. What the public record must now say

If GGAT02038s, or its successor identifier, still leads as a post-medieval farm or dwelling, it does not satisfy the function of a working historic environment record, and it is difficult to reconcile with section 194(2)(j) of the Historic Environment (Wales) Act 2023. I have not seen the source file, so I put that as a request for correction if the classification is as described by Cadw officers, not as a finding I have verified on the face of the record.

A professional user needs, in the principal description and not only in a later narrative paragraph: the 1974 measured survey; GGAT's 1978–80 work and 1982 advice; that the 1990 evaluation followed demolition and found human bone; that the 1994 excavation recovered the assemblage above, including in the 1990 low-potential zone; museum accessions 82.44H and
95.56H with their catalogued localities; and a note that the c.1880 NMW ironwork attribution is uncorroborated by the institution said to hold the object.

Please also reconcile the NGRs in use for the farmhouse, the 1990 trenches, the 1994 excavation, the churchyard and the development parcels. Distinguish this site from Great House Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge, and from Llandow. Two Llandoughs sit in the same historic county. Homonym error is a live records risk.

What I ask now

A. A complaint reference, the name of the person who will determine it, the procedure you will apply, the timescale, and any independent review route. Preserve all surviving Great House Farm records pending that determination.

B. Confirm which legal entity holds the records and functions formerly of GGAT Ltd, and who handles HER corrections.

C. Answer sections 1 to 10 from the documents you hold. Where a document does not survive, say when it left the file, under what retention rule, and by whose authority.

D. Correct the HER so that the 1979 and 1994 investigations and accessions
82.44H and 95.56H sit in the principal description, the 1880 attribution is qualified, the 1990 low-potential zone is annotated against the 1994 result, the three identifiers are reconciled, and Archwilio does not silently substitute another trust's site.

E. Test and, if confirmed, correct the Archwilio substitution.

F. If you accept any part of this complaint, say what remedy you offer:
record correction, release of surviving files or an index, a written account of the 1989–90 dual-role arrangement, and a methodological note on the 1990 evaluation against the 1994 excavation.

I do not ask you to adjudicate title. I do ask you to account for what GGAT knew, what it recorded, what it advised, what it then sold and executed, what was found four years later, what the national museum now catalogues from GGAT's own 1979 work, and whether the public record now tells the truth of that sequence.

This letter is sent so that Heneb and GGAT Ltd have a fair opportunity to investigate, answer, and offer remedy before any further process. Please answer each numbered section. A general assurance that the organisation acted appropriately will not do.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member [redacted]

Please visit
greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com

thread_title: FOI 2026-032 — other archaeological discoveries at Great House Farm and Church Farm
subject: RE: FOI - 2026-032 - Great House Farm, Llandough
body:
Dear FOI Team,

FOI 2026-032

Diolch yn fawr. Thank you for the records, the descriptors and the published references. This is a thorough response and it is genuinely useful.

One correction of place is required.

The request concerns Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough near Penarth / Cardiff. Among the disclosed PAS material is at least one record for a different property of the same name: Great House Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge (including 2022.18.1, NGR SS9934672805, medieval lead Romanesque mount). There is also a Great House farm entry at Llandow. Those are not the site named in the request. Two Llandoughs, and more than one Great House Farm, sit in the same county. The homonym is easy to miss and material.

Please treat the Cowbridge / Llandow entries as out of scope for this request unless you hold recorded information showing they were, at any time, indexed, cited, or treated as if they related to Great House Farm, Llandough (Penarth / Cardiff). If any such cross-attribution exists in historic files, catalogues, correspondence, or search notes, that recorded information is within scope and I ask that it be disclosed.

If labels or findspot fields are now amended to distinguish the two farms, please do not overwrite the original wording without retaining the prior form. I ask that any correction be recorded as a dated amendment, with the earlier descriptor preserved, so the sequence of how the records stood when searches were first run remains inspectable. Please do not destroy, weed, or replace the versions as disclosed on 22 September 2026.

One small point from my email of 26 August also remains. As item 7 I asked for any recorded information showing the basis on which the Museum concluded that the identified records were unrelated to the reported nineteenth-century discovery. If that conclusion was reached by staff judgement and not written down, please simply confirm that no recorded information is held on that point. I am not asking for a new opinion.

Could you also confirm the date by which you expect to respond to FOI 2026-036?

Cofion,

Sion Buckler
greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com

thread_title: Internal review 1188/26 of FOI 719/26
subject: Internal review of 719/26 (no records held) and overdue request of 20 August 2026 — Great House Farm, Llandough, 1988
body:
Freedom of Information / Data Management Team,

Request 719/26, and my request of 20 August 2026 (deaths of William Buckler
and Mary Doreen Williams)

1. Internal review of 719/26

I understand the Force's position is that it holds no records. I ask for an
internal review of that conclusion, because the search does not appear
capable of finding what the request describes.

South Wales Constabulary officers were present at the eviction and
demolition at Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough, between 29 November
and 6 December 1988. This is not a matter of recollection. It appears in
ITV Wales footage from the time, now public on ITV's archive channel, and
in contemporary newspaper photographs and reports, which I can supply. A
police presence on that scale would have generated records: a duty or
deployment record, an operational order or briefing, an occurrence or
incident log, liaison with the Under-Sheriff or bailiffs, press office
material, and possibly photographs.

For the review, please confirm in writing:

(a) Which systems, archives and paper holdings were searched, including
pre-1990s paper records of the former Penarth/Barry division and any South
Glamorgan command records.
(b) The search terms used. Records of that period may be indexed under
"Leckwith Road", "Llandough", "BP Properties", "Buckler", "Williams", "Ty
Mawr", "eviction", "breach of the peace" or the date, rather than "Great
House Farm".
(c) Whether records of that type from 1988 were destroyed under a retention
schedule, and if so which schedule and whether any disposal record survives.
(d) Whether any records were transferred to Glamorgan Archives or the South
Wales Police Heritage Centre, with the reference if known.

If records were destroyed, a record of their destruction is itself
information I am asking for. If they are held elsewhere, please tell me
where, under your duty to advise and assist.

I was present at the eviction as a child. So far as any record contains my
personal data, please also treat this as a subject access request under
Article 15 UK GDPR.

2. Request of 20 August 2026

This request was due on 18 September 2026 and I have had no response beyond
the automatic acknowledgement. Please give me its reference and the
response. If the records are not held, please say whether they were
destroyed or passed to the Coroner.

If I do not receive the internal review outcome within 20 working days, I
will complain to the Information Commissioner.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com

subject: Referral to the Independent Complaints Reviewer — HM Land Registry, titles WA231076 / WA240304 (Llandough)
body:
Dear Independent Complaints Reviewer,

Complaint about HM Land Registry — titles WA231076 and WA240304 (closed), land north of Leckwith Road, Llandough (Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr). HMLR references: N610CGV, 260919-6726246.

I ask you to review how HM Land Registry handled my complaint. HMLR gave its final decision on 25 May 2026 that the title was "registered correctly". I understand you cannot review that registration decision itself. My complaint is about the way it was reached and handled:

1. The decision came before the file was examined. HMLR gave its final decision on 25 May 2026, but did not list what the first-registration files actually contain until 30 July 2026. A final complaint decision cannot properly rest on documents that had not yet been identified.

2. The decision relies on a document that does not appear on the file. HMLR's letter of 19 April 2026 described a 15-year root of title. The root relied on, a conveyance of 31 December 1969, was under 13 years old at first registration in 1982. Neither that conveyance nor the 1971 abstract said to prove it appears on the 30 July 2026 file list, and HMLR has not explained this.

3. HMLR has given three different dates for the closure of title WA240304:
1983 (file correspondence of 12 April 1983), 1987 (an amalgamation application of 2 February 1987, made while my family's appeal was pending) and 2005 (an email of 21 September 2026). It has not reconciled them.

4. The stage 1 response relied on a form FR1 certificate, although the applications were on forms 1E and 1C.

5. The file holds examination material (form D23 and a letter of 8 April
1983) and two 1994 applications "to correct the title". HMLR has not explained any of them.

6. My written questions, including through my MP Stephen Doughty, have been redirected to a property search service instead of being answered.

The outcome I seek is a numbered written answer to these points, confirmation that all first-registration, amalgamation and correction records for both titles are being preserved, and acknowledgement of any failure in how the complaint was handled.

I am separately taking advice on whether to apply to alter the register. I understand that is outside your remit.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

thread_title: Independent Complaints Reviewer — referral ICR/090/26
subject: Re: Your complaint about HM Land Registry - referral to ICR Office
body:
Dear Ms Applegate,

Thank you for your letter of 28 September 2026 acknowledging my emails of 26 and 27 September, and for allocating reference ICR/090/26. I note that an investigation officer will contact me within ten working days.

I would like to place four further points on the file for the investigation officer, in addition to those already set out in my emails.

1. Public record

Please treat https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ as part of the material already cited.

The landing page sets out, diagrammatically and with links to the underlying evidence, the family’s case that Parcel A — the farmhouse, garden and associated land on the Williams/Thomas line — was included within a whole-farm registered title even though the documentary root by which BP acquired that parcel remains unresolved.

Our paper title deed being stolen from our home resulting in us not able to be present in court in 1974 (and so ownership adjudication was ajourned and our ownership assertion was weakened (not exstiguished) we understand. But the stretch of the imagine it takes to ever believe it was Western Ground Rents or BPs is all based on absurdity after absurdity and does not in my estimation, meet the criteria of what a sane, reasonable person would do.

The website greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com
deliberately distinguishes documentary records from family evidence, reconstruction and unresolved inference. I am therefore not asking ICR to accept every proposition on the site as established fact; I am asking that the underlying records and the specific questions identified there be considered.

2. Chronology now recorded by HM Land Registry

I had earlier written as if the two titles merged in 1983. That was wrong. HM Land Registry’s letter of 23 March 2026 (Lisa Griffiths, ref N610CGV) separates the first-registration events from the later amalgamation. My correction of 27 September is already on your file.

The chronology that now matters is:

• 30 November 1982 — application to first-register WA231076.

• 23 February 1983 — application to first-register WA240304.

• 26 March 1983 — Mary Williams died. Our family’s account is that notice of BP’s registration was received only after her death, during/ after that mourning period. Whether that account can be established from the notice, service and correspondence records is itself a question for investigation.

• 24 July 1986 — Hollis J. The historical title material still showed both titles live.

• 2 February 1987 — an application to amalgamate the two titles was recorded. WA240304 was subsequently closed and registration continued under WA231076. This is the amalgamation event, distinct from the 1982/83 first registrations. It occurred while the BP Properties Ltd v Buckler litigation was still live and before the Court of Appeal judgment of 31 July 1987.

• *14 April 1989 — Buckler v United Kingdom was declared inadmissible by the European Commission of Human Rights.*

I regard this as a further institutional failure that now requires reconsideration. The decision treated BP as having rights in our land parcel and referred to BP as the owners, although BP had been awarded possession, not ownership, and ownership of Parcel A had never been adjudicated in BP’s favour. The distinction is fundamental. Possession is not the same thing as ownership, and an order for possession did not itself determine that BP had acquired the underlying proprietary interest in Parcel A.

On the family’s case, our ownership claim to Parcel A was never extinguished. The question therefore is not simply whether BP obtained possession through the proceedings, but whether any legal process ever transferred, extinguished or superseded the family’s underlying proprietary interest. If it did not, the basis upon which BP was subsequently treated as having superior rights in the parcel requires examination.

That issue also goes directly to the later assertion that the family’s occupation became “permissive” under BP’s 1974 licence letters. A party cannot ordinarily confer a proprietary right it does not itself possess. If BP did not own Parcel A, it is necessary to establish what legal interest BP actually held that enabled it to grant my grandmother, or anyone else, permissive occupation of that parcel — particularly where there had already been a long succession of earlier attempts to establish a permissive basis for the family’s occupation.
The point is especially significant because the person whose occupation was supposedly made permissive was herself the long-standing occupier and, on the family’s case, the superior title holder of the parcel, with the family’s occupation extending back centuries. I therefore ask that the investigation distinguish carefully between *possession awarded to BP, ownership of Parcel A, and any alleged power to license the family’s occupation*. Those are not interchangeable propositions, and the documentary basis for treating them as such requires examination.

3. What I am asking ICR to review

HM Land Registry has told my MP, and said in its stage-two decision of 25 May 2026, that the title was registered correctly and that there is no evidence of a mistake. That is the institutional position my family has encountered for decades.

I am not asking ICR to determine title. I am asking whether that conclusion was reached after a proper examination of the first-registration files and, in particular:

• the documentary basis and extent claimed for Parcel A in the first-registration applications;

• the missing 31 December 1969 conveyance and the 1971 abstract of title;

• the notice and service records, including what notice was given to the occupier, when, and what effective opportunity existed to object;

• the three inconsistent closure dates now appearing in the HMLR record for WA240304; and

• the 2 February 1987 amalgamation application, including what was actually amalgamated, on what plans and documents, and what title information existed at that point in the still-live litigation.

The concern is therefore not simply one of hindsight. Much of the relevant material was created contemporaneously with the events in question. That is why I raise mistake, concealment and procedural unfairness as matters requiring investigation, rather than as findings I am asking you to make at this acknowledgement stage.

4. Why the record was reconstructed from Y Wladfa

For almost two years I have been in the Welsh Settlement in Patagonia, rebuilding a replica of the farmhouse in which I was born.

That reconstruction prompted me to revisit the documentary history of Great House Farm and, in doing so, to compare the family evidence with the surviving land-registration, court and archival records. That work is what brought the title chronology and the unresolved Parcel A question back into focus.

The replica is also a way of preserving the history of a house that was demolished in December 1988. I mention this not as an argument on the merits, but to explain why a historical record that had remained largely unexamined for decades was reconstructed now, and why I have pursued the underlying documents rather than relying solely on inherited family accounts.

Y Wladfa itself exists because Michael D. Jones and those who followed him judged that Welsh language, history, heritage, people, landscape and buildings were being overwritten in Wales — the process they cited as the work of a “decapitation committee”. Which makes it interesting 99% of UK MPs refused to sign an EDM in 2025 condemning us Christians being decapitated. Our land parcel was clearly a Christian stronghold and holy sacred lands and we were clearly stewards of it for centuries.

The Patagonia Welsh settlement is where those things are instead kept, celebrated and respected. The replica stands there for the same reason the original house cannot stand on Parcel A.

I will wait to hear from the investigation officer.

I also take this opportunity to draw your attention to the enclosed PDF, which contains photographs relating to a tree-planting ceremony on the southernmost part of our claimed Parcel A and subsequent photographs showing the tree being demolished. The ceremony is part of the family’s evidence of its assertion of ownership: my great-grandfather is recorded as planting the tree to commemorate that ownership. The photographs also preserve contemporaneous visual evidence, including identifiable individuals and machinery vehicle registration numbers, which may assist in establishing who carried out the later destruction and in what circumstances.

There is a further land-history issue which may be relevant to the wider question of how our claimed parcel came to be treated as no longer belonging to the family. The woodland to the north of our home, on our claimed parcel, was taken at a time when my grandmother had undergone a leg amputation in 1955 and had become wheelchair-bound. I understand that this woodland was subsequently gifted to a charity, which has itself contacted me recently; I enclose that correspondence with the present material.

Similarly, I understand that land to the south of the farmhouse was also taken, notwithstanding that the 1955 possession order appears, on the documentary material presently available to me, to have concerned the parcel to the east of ours. The Council subsequently made the southern land into a small green or park and, in the process, the commemorative tree and other physical evidence of the family’s assertion of ownership were destroyed. I appreciate that this moves beyond the immediate registration question, but the destruction of physical evidence bearing directly upon the family's historic claim may be relevant to understanding the subsequent evidential position.

There is also a further matter which I mention cautiously because I do not yet know its full significance. It has been alleged to me that the long-serving Council Clerk for Llandough played a role in the destruction of this evidence. When I initially raised the matter through FOI, his response was, as I understand it, an attempt not to become involved. When subsequently required to respond, he retired after approximately 35 years' service. I am not asserting that these events establish misconduct or that his retirement was connected with this matter; I do not presently know the extent, if any, of the connection.

I include the material because I believe it may have evidential relevance, whether to the immediate investigation or, if not, at a later stage when the wider history of the land and the disappearance of evidence is considered. The tree ceremony, its subsequent destruction, the photographs, and the associated correspondence provide material evidence which I do not think should be disregarded simply because some aspects of it may ultimately fall outside the immediate scope of this review.

There is also an important cultural dimension to the evidence. The tree was not merely a physical object: its planting appears to have been an act of asserting and commemorating ownership according to the family’s longstanding traditions and understanding of the land. I recognise that questions of ancient custom and tradition may not fall within the immediate legal scope of ICR/090/26. I mention them because the destruction of the physical manifestation of that assertion removed evidence of the very claim whose documentary survival is now being investigated.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/ Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

subject: Preservation notice — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — do not destroy records — Matter of public interest
note: Multi-authority preservation notice; HM Land Registry (FOI, Find a Property support and Customer Support) and the Independent Complaints Reviewer were among the copied recipients. Replies from other bodies are catalogued on their own pages.
body:
*FORMAL PRESERVATION NOTICE*
*Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth*
*Titles: WA231076, WA240304, WA513690 and WA735527*
*Planning references: 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES*

*URL: **greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com
<http://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com>*

*To each recipient separately, in your own capacity as a current or potential holder, custodian or controller of relevant records:*

This notice is addressed to each recipient *individually*. It is *not a joint request*, and it does not ask any recipient to speak for, investigate on behalf of, or answer in place of any other person or organisation. Each recipient is asked to respond only in respect of records within that recipient's own possession, custody or control, including records inherited from a predecessor organisation or retained on its behalf.
1. Nature and purpose of this notice

This is a *formal preservation notice* concerning documentary material relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's, and the subsequent development of the site, including the area now associated with Church View Close.

It is *not a claim form, is not service of proceedings, and is not intended to constitute or replace any FOI request, internal review, complaint, subject-access request or other statutory process already made to any recipient.*

The purpose of this notice is to require the preservation of potentially relevant material while the documentary history, title chain, registration history, planning history, possession proceedings, demolition and subsequent development are being reconstructed.

A separate first-stage preservation notice has been issued or is being issued to Cadw / Welsh Government FOI, HM Land Registry Wales Office and DPO, Heneb / GGAT HER, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan FOI Unit and DPO, Glamorgan Archives, South Wales Police FOI, The National Archives, the Wales Office FOI team, and the National Library of Wales. Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd has received a separate preservation letter.

*You are receiving this notice separately because the published documentary record places you, or a predecessor whose records may remain in your custody or control, within the documentary, legal, professional, administrative or development chain concerning this land.*
2. Land and documentary scope

Please preserve, and do not destroy, alter, overwrite, discard, transfer out of custody without a recorded handover, or otherwise dispose of, any record within your possession, custody or control relating to the land or matters identified below.

The scope includes, without limitation, *originals, copies, working papers, drafts, annotations, plans, photographs, negatives, films, tapes, maps, registers, indexes, correspondence, emails and attachments, electronic files, archived mailboxes, databases, metadata, internal notes, meeting records, instructions, client or matter files, survey material and other associated records.*

The material requested includes:

*1. Historical ownership, occupation and conveyancing*

The 1877 split; the 1916 and 1939 tenancies; the 1938 Bute to Western Ground Rents conveyance; the 1969 Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust conveyance; and any plans, schedules, abstracts, searches, correspondence or other documents relied upon in relation to those transactions.

*2. Possession proceedings and subsequent litigation*

The 1955 High Court and 1962 Cardiff County Court possession orders; the 1974 proceedings; *BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2*; House of Lords leave papers, including *YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536*; and *Buckler v United Kingdom (1989)*, including associated correspondence, instructions, evidence, plans and working papers.

*3. Land registration*

The first registration of *WA231076*, including the application dated 30 November 1982; the first registration of *WA240304*, including the application dated 23 February 1983; subsequent amalgamation, transfer or closure; and every plan, conveyance, abstract, search, application, correspondence trail or professional file relied upon in connection with those registrations or changes.

*4. 1988 possession and demolition*

The taking of possession on or about *29 November 1988* and the demolition commenced on or about *6 December 1988*, including any planning, listed-building, heritage, police, enforcement, media, contractor, survey, photographic or inter-agency liaison material.

*5. Planning and subsequent development, 1989–1996*

Planning application *89/01396/OUT*; reserved matters application *92/00671/RES*; conditions 16–18; GGAT / Cotswold Archaeology material; records concerning any *section 52, section 106, planning obligation, local land charge or equivalent instrument*; and the transfer from BP to Ideal Homes dated *3 December 1993*, together with all associated plans, correspondence, approvals, agreements, searches and completion material.

*6. Family records*

Records concerning *Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983)* and *William Buckler*, insofar as those records relate to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, the land described above, its occupation, ownership, possession, disposal, registration, development or demolition.
3. Predecessor and inherited files

Where you hold, or may hold, a file originating with a predecessor, successor, merged practice, affiliated practice, client or other entity, that material is also within scope.

This includes, without limitation, records originating from:

*Loosemores of Cardiff; Robbins Olivey & Blake Lapthorn / Blake Morgan; Linklaters & Paines; Debenham Tewson / DTZ / Cushman & Wakefield; Wyn Thomas + Partners; Ideal Homes Wales; BP Properties; BP Pension Trust; Cotswold Archaeological Trust; Cardiff Bay Development Corporation; and South Glamorgan County Council.*

The reference to a predecessor file does not assert that you necessarily hold such a file. It identifies material for which a reasonable custody or succession inquiry should be made where applicable.
4. Preservation steps

Please take reasonable steps to prevent the routine destruction, deletion, alteration or overwriting of potentially relevant material, including material held in *archived mailboxes, legacy systems, off-site storage, document-management systems, backup repositories and other electronic or physical stores*.

Where relevant material has been transferred to another repository, archive, successor organisation or third party, please preserve the information necessary to identify the transfer and its current location, including any accession, file, box, reference or custody details.

Nothing in this notice requires the creation of records that do not exist. The request concerns the preservation of records already held or controlled by you.
5. Purpose and legal position

This notice is *not a finding against any recipient*, and I am not asking any recipient to determine title or adjudicate the underlying dispute.

The *1987 Court of Appeal judgment* is relied upon here only for matters actually determined by that judgment, including the issues concerning possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. This preservation notice does not treat that judgment as having determined the complete documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel.

The underlying documentary history, including the relationship between the farmhouse parcel and the agricultural land subsequently dealt with through Western Ground Rents and BP, remains a matter requiring reconstruction from the primary records.

Accordingly, preservation is requested precisely so that the documentary record can be established from the records themselves rather than through assumptions based on later registration, later occupation, later planning treatment or secondary descriptions.
6. Acknowledgement and identification of records

Please acknowledge receipt of this notice and, in your own capacity, confirm:

*(a)* the officer, partner, records manager or other person responsible for implementing the preservation hold;

*(b)* what records within your possession, custody or control you have identified as falling within the scope above; and

*(c)* where you identify no records within scope, what relevant systems, files, repositories or predecessor records you searched in reaching that conclusion.

A substantive assessment of title is not requested from you. The immediate requirement is preservation and identification of the documentary material you hold.

The public documentary index and developing evidence record is available at:

*https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/
<https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/>*

Please monitor that site for subsequent identification of documents, references and specific schedules relevant to your organisation's records.

Where a reliable public email address is unavailable, a postal preservation notice will also be sent. For example, a postal notice will follow to *Loosemores,
Alliance House, 18–19 High Street, Cardiff CF10 1PT*.

Nothing in this notice constitutes an abandonment, waiver or limitation of any claim, position or remedy concerning *title, registration, concealment, limitation, reopening, rectification or alteration of the register, or any associated matter.*

Regards,

*Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)*
*Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member*

thread_title: Preservation notices and subject access request D260928 (28 September 2026)
subject: Subject access request — WA231076 / WA240304 — Great House Farm, Llandough — Williams / Buckler
body:
Data Protection Officer
HM Land Registry
dataprotection@landregistry.gov.uk
cc: Wales.Office@landregistry.gov.uk; FOI@landregistry.gov.uk Refs already with you: N610CGV; letter of SG Haste, 30 July 2026

Sirs/Madam,

Subject access request under UK GDPR Article 15.
Requester: Sion Buckler.
Titles: WA231076 and WA240304 (closed). Land north of Leckwith Road, Llandough (Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr).

This is not a request for an official copy of the register. It is a request for personal data in the working file in which I am identifiable, including customer-complaint files, the pack sent to Stephen Doughty MP, and any note of my correspondence on N610CGV.

Please also say whether the first-registration file contains personal data about Mary Doreen Williams (died 26 March 1983) or William Buckler, so far as you can disclose it to me as a family representative, and what identity you require before the month starts.

The matters to which that file goes, so you can search properly, are these. They are questions, not findings against Land Registry:

1. First-registration applications: WA231076 on 30 November 1982 (form 1E); WA240304 on 23 February 1983 (form 1C); later amalgamation and closure of WA240304.
2. A 31 December 1969 conveyance, Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust, identified as a root, and whether it is on the 30 July 2026 schedule of documents surviving on the file.
3. Notice and opportunity to object in 1982–83, while Mary Williams remained in occupation of the farmhouse. Family evidence is that notification was not received until after her death on 26 March 1983. I am seeking the notice and service record.
4. What the 1987 Court of Appeal decided (possession, limitation, October 1974 letters) and what it did not decide (documentary root of the farmhouse and garden parcel).

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ .

Please preserve the first-registration file and the complaint file. Do not start the statutory month until you have said what identification you need. thread_title: FOI/EIR 00211557 — s.52/land charges, planning register, condition 16–18 chain, 92/00671/RES; missing appendices C, D and E
subject: FOI/EIR — Great House Farm / Church View Close — s.52/land charges, planning register, EA screening, condition 16–18 chain, 92/00671/RES — new request, not 00210772
body:
Information Governance Team
Vale of Glamorgan Council
FoiUnit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk
cc: planning@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

Sirs/Madam,

New request under FOIA 2000 and/or EIR 2004. Do not treat this as a reopening or expansion of 00210772, 00211463 or 00211484. Those cases stay as they are.

Land: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Leckwith Road, Llandough, later Church View Close.
Applications: 89/01396/OUT (outline granted 13 March 1990) and 92/00671/RES.

I already have, or have already asked for, the officer's report, Policy H.2 text, Appendices C–E, the decision notices, and the general archaeological-condition papers. This request is confined to classes that those earlier requests did not name.

Please disclose recorded information held, or confirm item by item if not held:

1. Section 52 / later section 106 / land charges
Any agreement under section 52 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1971, any later section 106 instrument, any deed, undertaking or other agreement regulating the development or use of this land, and any corresponding entry on the local land charges register. Search legal, planning and land-charges holdings, not only the 2026 planning-file scan. If none is held, say so expressly. That is an open records question, not a conclusion that none existed.

2. Historic planning register
The planning-register entries that the Town and Country Planning General Development Order 1988 required the authority to keep for 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES: the applications, reserved-matters applications, plans and drawings, and relevant decision information. If the 2026 file disclosure is incomplete against that register, say what the register still lists and what is missing from the file.

3. Appendix B
Appendix B to the officer's report on 89/01396/OUT: the further GGAT comments after discussions with the Trust. Case 00211463 asked for C, D and E and for a list of annexes. It did not ask for B by that description. If B is not held, say when it left the file, under what retention rule, and whether any copy survives elsewhere.

4. Condition 16–18 chain
Named papers, not a general search:
(a) conditions 16, 17 and 18 as issued on the 13 March 1990 permission;
(b) the Council's October 1990 confirmation of condition 17;
(c) GGAT's archaeological warning of July 1992;
(d) the September 1992 reserved-matters approval, and whether any further archaeological condition was attached;
(e) the 1993–94 papers on whether condition 18 had been discharged, including GGAT's December 1993 letters recommending a breach-of-condition notice.

5. Environmental assessment / screening
Any preliminary environmental-assessment determination, screening opinion, or recorded decision that an environmental statement was or was not required for 89/01396/OUT. The application site is described as about 3.4 acres / 1.38 hectares. I am not asserting that an environmental statement was required. I am asking whether the Council made and recorded the determination at all.

6. Archaeological-interest consultation route
Any record of the statutory consultation route actually used because the land was recorded in the county Sites and Monuments Record, or was treated as a "site of archaeological interest" under the 1988 Order. I am not asking you to treat SMR status as automatic proof of a particular duty. I am asking what route was used.

7. Application receipt date
The Council's receipt record for 89/01396/OUT. The application form is dated October 1989. The reconstructed planning record gives 8 November 1989 as receipt of the application and plans. Please supply the date-stamped receipt, validation or register entry.

8. 92/00671/RES completeness and applicant standing
(a) A file list or register for 92/00671/RES showing what the reserved-matters file originally contained.
(b) Any sale, option, conditional-contract or authority-to-apply paper on the planning files covering the change from BP Properties (1989 outline applicant) to Ideal Homes Wales (appearing on the 1992 reserved-matters trail), including the recorded BP-to-Ideal Homes transfer of 3 December 1993.
This is a documentary interest/authority question. It is not an allegation that the 1992 application was invalid.

If a record is not held, say so for that item. If it was destroyed, transferred or archived, give the date, the schedule, and any surviving catalogue. Search planning, legal, land charges and archived/scanned holdings.

Please give a new reference and the 20 working-day date. Preserve anything in scope.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . I am not asking the Council to decide title.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals
[redacted]

subject: Formal concern, preservation and subject access — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — remedy before escalation
body:
Victoria Davidson
Monitoring Officer and Head of Legal and Democratic Services
Vale of Glamorgan Council
vdavidson@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk
Also: DPO@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk; complaints@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

Sirs/Madam,

This is a formal concern, a preservation notice, and a subject access request. It is the opportunity to remedy before the Information Commissioner and, if the internal processes end without remedy, the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales.

I am not asking the Council to decide title. I am asking it to deal with its own records and its own delay.

1. Complete the internal review of FOI/EIR 00210772, requested 7 July 2026, acknowledged 10 July 2026, further apology 11 September 2026, chased 5 August, 1 September and 22 September 2026. There is still no outcome. That is past a reasonable period. An ICO complaint confined to that delay is drafted. A completed review would deal with the point.

2. Preserve planning, building-control, housing, legal, local-land-charge and land records for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, titles WA231076 and WA240304, Church View Close, and the 1988 demolition (possession 29 November 1988; demolition begun 6 December 1988). Stop routine destruction of those files. That hold includes, if held:
- any section 52 TCPA 1971 / later section 106 / deed / undertaking and the matching land-charge entry;
- the 1988 GDO planning-register entries for 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES;
- officer-report Appendices B–E (B = further GGAT comments after discussions with the Trust);
- conditions 16–18 and the 1990–94 discharge papers, including the October 1990 confirmation of condition 17 and the 1993–94 dispute over condition 18;
- any environmental-assessment / screening determination for the outline application;
- the complete 92/00671/RES file and any BP–Ideal Homes sale, option or conditional-contract paper on the planning files, including the recorded transfer of 3 December 1993.
A separate FOI/EIR for those classes will follow and must not be folded into 00210772, 00211463 or 00211484.

3. Subject access under UK GDPR Article 15: personal data you hold about me, Sion Buckler, in those files, and about Mary Doreen Williams (died 26 March 1983) and William Buckler so far as the law allows a relative to see it. Say what identification you need before the month starts.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . The investigation distinguishes Parcel A (farmhouse, garden, buildings and yard — the family's maintained freehold) from Parcel B (eastern fields — not presently disputed). The 1987 Court of Appeal decided possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. It did not decide the documentary root of Parcel A. Council papers on planning and demolition go to that question. They are not a finding against any officer.

Nothing in this letter abandons any claim concerning title, registration, concealment, limitation, reopening or reparations. This is not a claim form.

Please acknowledge, name the officer for the hold, and give a date for the 00210772 outcome.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals

body:
Freedom of Information
Welsh Government
Freedom.ofinformation@gov.wales
cc: walesofficefoi@ukgovwales.gov.uk — so 26FOI 103 stays on the same fact

Sirs/Madam,

Request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000.
Requester: Sion Buckler.

Wales Office, in 26FOI 103 dated 22 September 2026, said historic Welsh Office / Cadw listing papers for this house sit with you. This is that request. I am not asking you to decide title.

Please disclose recorded information held by the Welsh Government or by Cadw as part of it concerning:

1. Any consideration, between 1 July and 31 December 1988, of listing, spot-listing or emergency listing of Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's (approx. ST 168 733).
2. Any inspection, photograph, minute or note of the building, or of its demolition, in that period. Possession was taken on 29 November 1988. Demolition of the farmhouse began on 6 December 1988.
3. Any transfer, destruction or disposal of those files, with the schedule used and the date.

If nothing is held, please say what was searched, including Cadw listing files, Welsh Office inherited files, and any index of destroyed building records.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . The investigation distinguishes Parcel A (farmhouse, garden, buildings and yard — the family's maintained freehold) from Parcel B (eastern fields — not presently disputed). The 1987 Court of Appeal decided possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. It did not decide whether the documentary root of Parcel A was ever established. These papers go to that question. They are not a finding against Cadw.

Thank you for contacting HM Land Registry. This is an automated response to confirm that we have received your correspondence. We aim to formally provide an acknowledgement within three working days. If you have any special requirements that mean you would like us to communicate with you in a specific way, please let us know and we will make adjustments if we can.

If you are contacting us in respect of any matters relating to property registration or have a general customer enquiry – Our team are unable to respond to any general registration enquiries or provide updates on any property applications. Please redirect your customer enquiry to our Customer Support colleagues, using any of the methods below:

  * Online contact form: HM Land Registry Contact Us form<https://customerhelp.landregistry.gov.uk/guide-page-external/?stepid=2b31bc48-eb96-eb11-b1ac-002248413956>

  * Website - www.gov.uk/guidance/contact-hm-land-registry<https://www.gov.uk/guidance/contact-hm-land-registry>

  * Telephone

     * English language 0300 006 0411

     * Welsh language 0300 006 0422

Telephone lines are open between 08:00 and 17:00 Monday to Thursday. This does not include Bank Holidays.

  * Post - HM Land Registry Citizen Centre

PO Box 74

Gloucester
GL14 9BB

There is no direct contact e-mail address for Customer Support. Please use the online contact form and any responses will be issued via e-mail.

If you have made a request under the Freedom of Information Act or Environmental Information Regulations–The statutory timescale for response is 20 working days following receipt of your request.

If you have made a request in relation to your data rights, for example, a subject access request for personal data – The statutory timescale for response is one calendar month following receipt of your request.

Please note that where personal data is held on our register, it is exempt from the right of subject access under UK GDPR.

Where any personal data is held on record for a registered title, the exemption provided at Schedule 2, Part 1, Paragraph 5(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018 would be engaged. 

This states: 

“5(1) The listed GDPR provisions do not apply to personal data consisting of information that the controller is obliged by an enactment to make available to the public, to the extent that the application of those provisions would prevent the controller from complying with that obligation.” 

Please see the section below titled 'Register information and your data protection rights' for further explanation.

If you have only copied your correspondence to us - we will not respond.

Yours sincerely

Information Rights Team

HM Land Registry

Register information and your data protection rights    

Data protection law permits HM Land Registry to use personal data for our official purposes.

The lawful basis for HM Land Registry processing personal data under the United Kingdom (UK) General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) is that it is necessary to enable us to perform our public task of the registration of land and property (Article 6(1)(e) of UK GDPR). This is defined in the Land Registration Act 2002. 

Paragraph 5 of Schedule 2 Part 1 of the Data Protection Act 2018 provides the following exemption from the specified UK GDPR provisions:

“The listed UK GDPR provisions do not apply to personal data consisting of information that the controller is obliged by an enactment to make available to the public, to the extent that the application of those provisions would prevent the controller from complying with that obligation.”    

The Land Registration Act 2002 is the principal legislation governing land registration in England and Wales. It sets out provisions for the keeping of a register of title to land and requirements for its administration by HM Land Registry under a Chief Land Registrar.

The Chief Land Registrar is required by the Land Registration Act 2002 and to make register information (including any documents held on the register of title) available to the public, therefore the following data protection provisions do not apply:

  * the requirement to provide ‘privacy notices’ to individuals

  * the requirement to provide personal data in response to subject access requests

  * the requirement to rectification

  * the requirement to comply with requests to erasure (right to be ‘forgotten’)

  * most of the principles of UK GDPR

Please visit our website for further information about our registers:

www.gov.uk/get-information-about-property-and-land<http://www.gov.uk/get-information-about-property-and-land>

For further information in relation to your rights and how HMLR processes personal data please refer to our Personal Information Charter:

www.gov.uk/government/organisations/land-registry/about/personal-information-charter<http://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/land-registry/about/personal-information-charter>

HM Land Registry’s purpose is to protect your land ownership and provide services and data that underpin an efficient and informed property market. Our vision is: “A world-leading property market as part of a thriving economy and a sustainable future”.

thread_title: Subject access, crime-recording request and search note on 719/26
subject: Subject access, crime-recording request, and search note on 719/26 — Great House Farm, Llandough, 1988
body:
Freedom of Information / Data Management / Crime Recording
South Wales Police
information@south-wales.police.uk
cc: Stephen Doughty MP — constituency record only. Please do not treat the copy as a further request to the MP.

Sirs/Madam,

This is separate from the internal review of 719/26 sent on the morning of 27 September 2026. Please do not merge them.

I am not asking you to decide the civil claim. I am asking you to apply the recording rules, and to disclose personal data.

1. Subject access, UK GDPR Article 15. Personal data you hold about me, Sion Buckler, arising from the eviction and demolition at Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, between 29 November and 6 December 1988, and from later correspondence including 719/26 and the request of 20 August 2026 concerning the deaths of William Buckler and Mary Doreen Williams. Say what identification you need before the month starts.

2. Crime recording. Please record, or explain in writing why you will not record, a report of suspected fraud and concealment in the creation and use of title to that land, including first registration of WA231076 (application 30 November 1982) and WA240304 (application 23 February 1983), and the 1987 proceedings. The question is whether a crime record should be opened. It is not a request that you find the civil title.

3. Search note on 719/26. “No records held” for a documented multi-officer operation in November–December 1988 still requires a note of systems searched, years searched, and whether South Wales Constabulary paper has gone to Glamorgan Archives. That note can sit with the internal review. I ask for it here so the crime-recording decision is not made without it.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . The 1987 Court of Appeal decided possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. It did not decide the documentary root of the farmhouse parcel. These are evidential questions. They are not a finding against any officer.

Please preserve any 1988 operational file, pocket book, custody record or transfer list. Nothing in this letter abandons any claim. This is not a claim form.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals
[redacted]

subject: Formal complaint — overdue subject access request arising from FOI2026/09019 — identity sent 5 August 2026
body:
Data Protection Officer
Ministry of Defence
APC-Sp-ParlDiscl-Triage-Mailbox@mod.gov.uk

Sirs/Madam,

Please pass this to the data-protection officer. This is a complaint about an overdue subject access request. It is not a repeat of the chase sent on the morning of 27 September 2026, and it is not a new Freedom of Information request.

FOI2026/09019, made on WhatDoTheyKnow, asked about any armed-forces involvement in the 1988 eviction at Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough. The FOI answer was that no information was held on the non-section-23 parts, and section 23(5) neither-confirm-nor-deny on Special Forces. I requested an internal review on 20 June 2026 and asked that personal data be dealt with as a subject access request off that public thread. Your own note was that the SAR should come by a private route. It did. Identity was sent on 5 August 2026. The UK GDPR month ended on 5 September 2026. There has been no disclosure, no extension, and no refusal.

I complain that the Ministry has not complied with Articles 12 and 15.

Within 14 days, please:

1. Send the personal data, or a refusal naming the exemption and the right to complain to the Information Commissioner.
2. Say what systems were searched for data relating to me, as a child in that household in 1988, as distinct from the FOI search already described (Restore, CT&UK, Army, and the keyword list on the review file).
3. Confirm the file is preserved.

If that is not done by 12 October 2026 I will complain to the Information Commissioner. This letter is the complaint to the organisation which the Commissioner expects first.

I do not assert that a unit was deployed. The FOI answer does not establish that either. The open question is whether any record names me. The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ .

Nothing in this letter abandons any claim. This is not a claim form. Do not publish identity documents.

thread_title: EIR 00210772 — internal review and formal chases
subject: [1] RE: Great House Farm, Llandough – Request 00210772 – Internal Review – Formal Chase
body:
Information Governance Team,

*Case Ref 00210772 — internal review requested 7 July 2026*

Thank you for your email of 11 September. You said that you would try to
update me by the end of the following week with a clearer timeframe. I have
not received that update.

Under regulation 11(4) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004,
an internal review should be completed as soon as possible and no later
than 40 working days after receipt of the request for reconsideration. On
my calculation, that period expired on 2 September 2026. The review is
therefore now overdue.

I appreciate that further historical documentation has been located and
that you may need to consult third parties. I am not asking you to
compromise any proper consultation process. However, I ask that you now
provide the following by *Tuesday 6 October 2026*:

1. *A firm date* by which the completed internal review decision will be
issued.

2. *A non-disclosive description of the further documentation located*,
including, so far as presently known:
- its approximate date or date range;
- who created or supplied it;
- how it came into the Council's possession; and
- approximately how many documents are involved.

I am asking for a description of the material and its provenance, rather
than disclosure of its substantive contents.

3. *Confirmation that the newly located documentation is being preserved in
its present form*, without alteration, destruction or disposal, while
the internal review and any subsequent complaint to the Information
Commissioner remain outstanding.

4. *Release now of any material that can properly be disclosed without
awaiting third-party consultation*, where the Council has already
established that no exemption or other restriction prevents disclosure.

If I do not receive a substantive response by *6 October 2026*, I will
refer the continuing delay to the Information Commissioner's Office without
further notice.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: Cadw — Formal complaint of 17 September 2026, re-service and supplement
subject: [2] Re: Supplement to complaint re-served 20 September 2026 — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough
body:
Dr Wigley / Cadw Complaints Manager,

This is not a new complaint and not a chase. It is notice for the stage-one complaint already opened under ticket #628635887: complaint of 17 September 2026, re-served on 20 September after delivery to cadw@gov.wales was rejected, with a supplement sent on 22 September.

The complaint is that Cadw’s 1988 assessment of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth (approximately ST 1681 7331; later HER GGAT02038s), did not adequately address the historic fabric, archaeological context and information then available, and that the building was demolished in December 1988 before any listing protection was secured.

I am not asking Cadw to determine title. I am asking Cadw to answer for its own role, decisions and professional handling of the 1988 assessment.

What I seek from this complaint, if Cadw is willing to resolve it without referral to the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales, is:

1. A written stage-one decision on whether Cadw’s 1988 assessment was adequate having regard to the material then available and the criteria and process applicable at the time, including the relevant 1979 GGAT excavation record concerning the Roman villa and associated early-medieval archaeology on land formerly within the farm holding.

2. If Cadw concludes that the assessment was inadequate, a written acknowledgement of that finding, confined to Cadw’s own role and without determination of title or third-party liability.

3. Cadw’s confirmation of whether it will ask Heneb to review HER entry GGAT02038s and, where necessary, correct or supplement the entry so that the relevant excavated archaeology is accurately recorded, rather than leaving the site classified simply as “POST MEDIEVAL – Farm” where that description is incomplete.

4. Confirmation of what records from the 1988 assessment Cadw still holds, what material was destroyed, disposed of or not retained, and the applicable retention schedule or rule governing the 1988 file.

I do not expect Cadw to rebuild the house or determine the separate title dispute involving HM Land Registry or any successor in title. Those matters belong to other processes.

I will await the stage-one response. I will not add further correspondence to this complaint unless Cadw asks a question or the published response timescale expires.

Please treat ticket #628635887 together with the emails of 17, 20 and 22 September 2026 as the complaint. This letter adds no new grounds.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: Welsh Government — Ministerial correspondence: Historic Environment Record statutory notice (TO/HF/05677/26)
subject: Re: Statutory notice under Historic Environment (Wales) Act 2023 ss.194–195 — HER GGAT02038s still classifies Wales’s largest excavated early-medieval cemetery as “POST MEDIEVAL – Farm”
note: The letter of 20 September 2026 that this email supplements was not found in the family mailbox when this page was compiled.
body:
Dear Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport,

This is a short supplement to my letter of 20 September 2026 on the historic environment record for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough (NPRN 20182; HER GGAT02038s). It does not replace that letter. It does not ask you to adjudicate title.

Three corrections to the letter of 20 September

1. A sentence in the middle of that letter was left unfinished. Please disregard it. Nothing in the requests depends on it.

2. The HM Land Registry letter forwarded by the constituency MP was dated 18 September 2026, not “yesterday”. On 27 September I wrote separately to HM Land Registry to correct a year I had used in earlier correspondence about titles WA231076 and WA240304. That correction is not a request to you.

3. I asked whether guidance under section 196 had been issued. Cadw’s published page now states that Historic Environment Records in Wales:
Compilation and Use (2017) is issued as statutory guidance under section 196 of the 2023 Act. What I still need is confirmation whether that 2017 text has been substantively reviewed since sections 194 to 196 came into force on 4 November 2024, and the date on which the current guidance was issued under section 196 and laid before Senedd Cymru. I would also be grateful for confirmation whether the current guidance addresses primary classification of records and the behaviour of the public interface.

What has happened since 20 September, relevant to the duties

On 27 September I made a formal complaint to Heneb concerning the HER identifiers, classification and the 1978–1995 record. Steven Foulston acknowledged it on 29 September as investigating officer, with a five-week target. That is Heneb’s own process. It does not discharge the Ministers’ duties under sections 194 and 195.

On 29 September the Royal Commission (RC26-0375) supplied the core description it says is used for GGAT02038s on Archwilio. That description is of a post-medieval farmhouse and barn. It records medieval finds, the 1974 survey and the demolition of 6 December 1988. The live HER also links the site to the separate 1994 excavation event, GGATE003875, which contains the excavation details and findings.

The adequacy question in my letter of 20 September can therefore be put more precisely: whether the HER, taken as a whole, provides the details of relevant investigations and their findings required by section 194(2)(j), and whether the way those records are classified, linked and presented publicly is sufficient for that purpose.

Cadw’s stage-one complaint on the 1988 listing decision remains open (ticket #628635887). That is a separate file. I mention it only so the two are not confused. The latest position is that the complaints investigation has commenced.

The five requests in the letter of 20 September stand. The one that can be tested immediately remains the Archwilio silent-substitution question:
whether an unresolved HER reference can silently resolve to a different record without warning.

I will work to the published seventeen-working-day response aim from 20 September. If a substantive response will take longer, I would be grateful simply to be told.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
