thread_title: Chase and further information — Great House Farm / suspected historic fraud
subject: Re: Great House Farm / suspected historic fraud — further information and request for consideration
note: This email opens 'Further to my email of earlier today'; no earlier email of 30 September 2026 to the CPS was found in the family's mailbox.
body:
Dear Mr/Ms Rutter,

Further to my email of earlier today and your message of 29 September 2026.

I am writing to place further material and context before the Victim Liaison Unit so that CPS Cymru-Wales has the information necessary to identify any existing record or referral and, where appropriate, to ensure that the material reaches the prosecutor or team responsible for considering it.

I am not asking the CPS to determine the underlying civil title to the property. The issue I am raising is whether the documentary history gives rise to potential criminal offences, whether those matters warrant investigation, and, if a private prosecution is subsequently instituted, whether the circumstances are such that the Director's power under section 6(2) of the Prosecution of Offences Act 1985 should be considered.

1. Police engagement and current references

On 28 September 2026 I submitted a formal crime-recording request to South Wales Police (information@south-wales.police.uk), copied to Stephen Doughty MP for constituency-record purposes only.

The request asks South Wales Police to record, or explain in writing why they will not record, a report concerning suspected fraud and related concealment in the creation and subsequent use of registered title to the former Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough. It identifies, in particular, the first-registration application for WA231076 dated 30 November 1982, the application for WA240304 dated 23 February 1983, and matters arising from the subsequent 1987 proceedings.

I also have a live Subject Access Request with South Wales Police concerning the 1988 eviction and demolition and related personal data.

I previously reported suspected irregularities concerning the 1982 registration to HM Land Registry (reference 260202-5732372). Further HM Land Registry enquiry references include 260929-6766714 and related references generated in September 2026.

If a Report Fraud reference is issued, I will provide it immediately. For present purposes, I ask that the South Wales Police crime-recording request and the HM Land Registry report of suspected registration irregularities be treated as the principal current investigative references.

2. Documentary title sequence and suspected criminality

The public evidence index is available at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

The material assembled there identifies a documentary sequence which, in my present assessment, raises questions as to whether the family's historic proprietary interest in the farmhouse parcel was displaced through the use of records, possession evidence and registration material relating to a different or wider parcel, and whether subsequent registration and dealings then relied upon that resulting title position.

For convenience, I refer on the website to this as the "synthetic title" issue. That is a description of the documentary pattern I have identified, rather than an assumption that criminal liability has already been established.

The distinction is important because the 1987 Court of Appeal proceedings concerned possession, limitation and the October 1974 correspondence. My concern is that those proceedings did not determine the underlying documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel now represented by the registered title history.

3. 1955 possession order and the neighbouring parcel

A further issue requiring examination is the relationship between the 1955 possession order and the land historically occupied and claimed by the Williams/Buckler family.

My evidence indicates that the 1955 order related to a neighbouring parcel rather than the family's core farmhouse holding. I am concerned that subsequent possession and development activity may nevertheless have treated that order, or the associated possession history, as extending to land outside the parcel to which it actually related.

Recent excavation and works on the former family land make this a live evidential issue. I ask that the underlying order, plans, descriptions and subsequent land use be considered against the documentary title sequence rather than assuming that the parcels were identical.

4. Possible loss or destruction of relevant records

I hold dated photographs concerning works which removed a commemorative tree planted by my great-grandfather on or adjoining the former Great House Farm / Church View Close land.

I have made a narrowed FOI request to the Vale of Glamorgan Council (case 00211484) seeking the instruction, works order, authorisation and any record linking the tree to the Williams/Buckler family or to the 1988 demolition.

More generally, I am concerned that parts of the planning and land-history record which could bear upon the ownership history are incomplete or unavailable. I am not presently asking the CPS to draw an inference from that absence. I ask that any potentially relevant records held by public authorities or other custodians be identified and preserved while the police and other investigations are ongoing.

5. Existing correspondence and preservation

I have maintained a continuous documentary record of communications concerning these issues with:

- South Wales Police, including FOI, SAR, crime-recording and preservation correspondence;
- HM Land Registry and the Independent Complaints Reviewer (ICR/090/26);
- Cadw, Heneb, RCAHMW, Glamorgan Archives, National Library of Wales and other heritage bodies; and
- Vale of Glamorgan Council, including FOI requests and internal reviews.

Preservation requests/notices have also been made to principal record-holders where I consider material may be relevant, so that potentially significant evidence is not inadvertently destroyed, transferred or disposed of while these matters are being examined.

6. Request to CPS Cymru-Wales

I respectfully ask CPS Cymru-Wales to:

(a) note the South Wales Police crime-recording request of 28 September 2026 and HM Land Registry reference 260202-5732372 as the present principal references, with any subsequent police or Report Fraud reference to be added when available;

(b) ensure that the material is considered by the appropriate CPS prosecutor or team if it is referred for prosecutorial consideration, including consideration of whether the alleged documentary conduct raises sufficiently serious or complex criminal issues to require specialist casework;

(c) note that, should a private prosecution subsequently be instituted, I may make a specific request for the CPS to consider the Director's power under section 6(2) of the Prosecution of Offences Act 1985; and

(d) advise me of the appropriate procedure for making such a request, and the evidence CPS would require, if that stage is reached.

I appreciate that the CPS does not itself conduct the police investigation. My purpose at this stage is to ensure that the potential prosecutorial dimension is properly identified and that the present material is capable of being matched to any police investigation or later referral.

I remain ready to provide an indexed evidential bundle comprising the 1955 and 1974 material, historical conveyances and plans, HM Land Registry documentation for WA231076, WA240304 and related titles, relevant court records, chronology, and photographs concerning the former property and subsequent works. The website provides a public index to much of this material.

I note the previous deadline of 13 October 2026. I will provide any South Wales Police crime/incident reference or Report Fraud reference as soon as it is allocated.

Yours sincerely,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: Formal complaint — HER identifiers and the 1978–1995 record (investigating officer Steven Foulston)
subject: [3] Re: Formal complaint — GGAT / Heneb: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — HER identifiers and the 1978–1995 record
body:
Mr Foulston,

Thank you for acknowledging the complaint of 27 September 2026 and for confirming you are the investigating officer. I note the five-week target.

Please treat this email as a supplement to that complaint. The attached is my report of GGATs involvement to the extent I know and a current consolidated account of GGAT’s role as curator, advisor, contractor and record-holder at Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough, and of the record now held by Heneb.

Attachment
GGAT — Forensic Critique, Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough, Version 4.0.3 (Final), 30 September 2026.

My AI agent generated report based on the info I hold thus far, does attempt to distinguish established facts, reasonable inferences, matters that cannot be established, and facts that cut against the criticism. I took care not to allege dishonesty, bad faith or criminal conduct by named officers. It records nine defects: the standing building; the 1982–1988 SMR gap; an evaluation method mismatched to GGAT’s own predictive model; specify-price-bid-execute on the same application; a missing representation from a County Councillor identified as a member of GGAT; access converted into a “non-existent to low” zoning; failure to answer the Disused Burial Grounds question GGAT itself raised; a still-misclassified and inconsistently identified HER; and the absence, until your appointment, of any substantive institutional answer.

What I ask Heneb to do on this complaint

1. Give me a complaint reference and confirm the target date for a written response.

2. Confirm which legal entity now holds GGAT’s records for this site (Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Limited, company 01276976 / charity 505609 / Heneb operationally).

3. Correct or formally review HER GGAT02038s, which remains classified as “POST MEDIEVAL – Farm” despite the 1994 cemetery and the 2005 publication of 1,026 burials as the largest early-medieval burial population then recovered in Wales.

4. Reconcile the HER identifiers already supplied to the family (including GGAT02038s, GGAT03586s and GGATE003872) and supply the source file, not a public summary.

5. Search and disclose, or certify as not held: file S387; the 1 October 1982 letter; the 1989 consultee report on 89/01396/OUT; the 8 February 1990 further comments (Appendix B to the officer’s report); the 1990 assessment archive; any emergency building record, watching brief or fabric report on the December 1988 demolition; and any conflicts register or trustee minute for the 1989–90 commission.

6. Address the nine criticisms in the attached report in writing.

Our family’s wider case, so the complaint is not read as a cataloguing dispute only

Separately from the archaeological record:

I believe there has been fraud, concealment and government involvement resulting in the dispossession of our home and land. The family has occupied and claimed Great House Farm since at least 1667. In 1988, after BP Properties Ltd v Buckler, we were removed. The farmhouse was demolished on 6 December 1988. About twenty houses now stand on that ground. The narrative that followed treated us as peasant squatters evicted from an old farmhouse. That narrative is false.

In reconstructing the house as a Welsh heritage museum in Patagonia I found that our ownership of the house-and-garden parcel was never extinguished. The working case is two parcels: Parcel A (house and garden) belonging to Mary Williams; Parcel B treated as if it were the whole farm; a synthetic title built by decades of false assertion that occupation of Parcel A was permissive. Limitation is postponed if concealment is made out.

That title case is for the Land Registry, the courts and the other bodies already on notice. It is not for Heneb to adjudicate. It is why the archaeological record matters. The same ground GGAT evaluated as largely empty contained inhumations a few centimetres below the topsoil. RCAHMW’s own file records that the standing building remained partially recorded because of the ownership dispute, and was then destroyed.

Our family has suffered shame, dispossession, ostracisation, exile, reputational harm, and the loss of our ancestral home, land and an incompletely recorded building. There were, on our case, serious human-rights failures in how that was done too. Such as my pregnant mum being thrown over the gateway of our property into a puddle, which is why she is in a sling with a dislocated collar bone on ITV News Wales footage afterwards. She was trying to get medicine for my father who lay in hospital after a heart attack. I watched helpless, as a child, while our home was demolished in front of us.

I am giving each institution that held a public function over this site the opportunity to remedy what it accepts. For Heneb that means putting the record right, producing what it holds, and saying plainly where GGAT’s 1978–1995 conduct and the present HER fail the standards that applied then and apply now. Remedy from Heneb is correction of the record, disclosure, and an accountable written position — not a finding on title.

Please confirm receipt of the attached report and that it forms part of the complaint file you are investigating.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

body:
Dear Mr Buckler,

ATISN 27589 - Great House Farm, Llandough

Thank you for your request which I received on 29 September. You asked for:

  1. Any consideration, between 1 July and 31 December 1988, of listing, spot-listing or emergency listing of Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's (approx. ST 168 733).
  2. Any inspection, photograph, minute or note of the building, or of its demolition, in that period. Possession was taken on 29 November 1988. Demolition of the farmhouse began on 6 December 1988.
  3. Any transfer, destruction or disposal of those files, with the schedule used and the date.

You will receive a response by 26 October 2026. If you have any queries about this request, please do not hesitate to contact me at the address below. Please remember to quote the reference number above in any future correspondence.

The request you sent me contains personal information about you - for example, your name and address. The Welsh Government will be the data processor for this information and, in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation, it will be processed in order to fulfil our public task and meet our legal obligations under the Act to provide you with a response. We will only use this personal information to deal with your request and any matters which arise as a result of it. We will keep your personal information and all other information relating to your request for three years from the date on which your request is finally closed. Your personal information will then be disposed of securely.

Under data protection legislation, you have the right:

• to be informed of the personal data we hold about you and to access it

• to require us to rectify inaccuracies in that data

• to (in certain circumstances) object to or restrict processing

• for (in certain circumstances) your data to be ‘erased’

• to (in certain circumstances) data portability

• to lodge a complaint with the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) who is our independent regulator for data protection

thread_title: Cadw — ATISN 27589: Welsh Office / Cadw papers, July–December 1988
subject: Re: FOI — Welsh Office / Cadw papers, July–December 1988 — Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough — following 26FOI 103 (ATISN 27589)
body:
Dear Dr Wigley,

Thank you for your acknowledgement of ATISN 27589 and confirmation that a response is due by 26 October 2026.

For the avoidance of doubt, I should clarify the two historical dates reproduced in your acknowledgement:

“Possession was taken on 29 November 1988” and “Demolition of the farmhouse began on 6 December 1988” were included in my request as contextual information identifying the period and events to which the requested records relate. Their repetition in the acknowledgement should not be treated as an acceptance by me that either date, or any legal characterisation of possession or demolition, has been established by the Welsh Government or by me. This whole situation maybe unprecedented. It was already a landmark legal case in 1987, without this added layer we may now be understanding.

My request is for recorded information held by the Welsh Government/Cadw concerning the matters specified in points 1–3. I am not asking Cadw to determine title, possession, limitation or any other legal issue, and nothing in this FOI correspondence is intended to constitute an admission, waiver, settlement or abandonment of any rights or position concerning those matters.

Please also expressly confirm that records falling within the scope of ATISN 27589, including any relevant historic listing, inspection, photographic, administrative and file-disposal records, will be preserved pending completion of the request and any applicable internal review or complaint process.

I look forward to the substantive response by 26 October. And sincerely thank you for your time and attention in this matter. You are appreciated.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant) Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: FOI 2026-036 — schedule of all Great House Farm / Church Farm records and 1875–1915 registers
subject: FW: 2026-036- Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff
note: The two schedules in this email were tables; their cells are shown one per line as they appear in the plain-text email.
body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your request.

Amgueddfa Cymru has previously responded to requests concerning Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Llandough Farm, Llandough, including FOI 2026-024 and FOI 2026-032. In responding to the present request, further enquiries were undertaken with Archaeology, Industry and Social History Collections. These enquiries built upon the searches already undertaken for the earlier requests.

Collections staff reviewed records identified through references to Great House Farm, Ty Mawr and Llandough Farm, Llandough (Vale of Glamorgan), together with records returned through associated place-name searches. Records relating to the wider Llandough area, to other locations sharing the name "Llandough", or to other properties bearing the name "Great House Farm" were reviewed but were not considered to relate to the location specified in your request.

Question 1
A schedule of every object, archive file, accession, loan, enquiry or correspondence record that Amgueddfa Cymru holds which is indexed, provenanced or otherwise recorded as from Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Llandough Farm, Llandough (Penarth / Vale of Glamorgan).
The schedules provided in response to FOI 2026-032 contained the records previously identified as relating to the location specified in your request.
The additional enquiries undertaken for this request identified the following records:
Reference
Title
Date
Description
Ref 13.2
Waterwheel from Llandough Farm
Collected 1 April 1979
Waterwheel collected from Llandough Farm. Museum records state that the item was donated by Wales and West Housing Association in connection with development of the site. The item was never formally accessioned and has subsequently been deaccessioned.
MS 3360/3
Particulars, Conditions and Plans of the Sale of Nine Well-Known Farms in the Vale of Glamorgan forming part of the Llandough Estate
1924
Photostat copy. Collections staff identified a page relating to Great House Farm within the document. Provided in FOI: 2026-032
No further records relating specifically to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Llandough Farm, Llandough were identified.

Question 2
The same schedule for Church Farm, Llandough, but only insofar as records were retrieved during the searches undertaken for FOI 2026-024 and can be identified without a new full search.
The record identified is:
Reference
Title
Description
63.24
Archaeological accession
Details attached
No further records were identified from the material retrieved during the searches undertaken for FOI 2026-024.

Question 3
Any accession, register entry, day-book, donations book or correspondence in the collections of Amgueddfa Cymru or of its predecessor Cardiff Museum / Welsh Museum of Natural History / National Museum of Wales, dated 1875-1915, recording ironwork, armour, a visor, a lance, a helmet, "armour from Llandough", or a find from Great House / Llandough Farm.
No such records were identified.

For clarification, the accession registers maintained by Cardiff Museum form the earliest accession registers of the National Museum of Wales collection. Objects held by Cardiff Museum were not re-accessioned when responsibility for the collections transferred to the National Museum of Wales and the accession numbering sequence continued uninterrupted. Searches of the earliest accession registers therefore encompass the former Cardiff Museum accession records.

As part of the enquiries undertaken in response to this request and previous requests concerning the same location, accession records and associated collections documentation were reviewed for the objects and locations specified above. No accession record, register entry, day-book entry, donations book entry or correspondence dated between 1875 and 1915 relating to finds from Great House Farm, Ty Mawr or Llandough Farm was identified.

Question 4
Any object record for Llandough ironwork that is not labelled "visor" or "lance" but is or was associated with the farmhouse floor or rear wing / dairy.
No such records were identified.

Archaeology Collections have confirmed that they hold no record of any additional ironwork from Llandough associated with the farmhouse floor, rear wing or dairy beyond material already considered in previous responses concerning this location.

I hope this information is helpful.

If you are dissatisfied with the way your request has been handled, you may request an internal review. Requests for an internal review should be submitted within 40 working days of the date of this response.

If you remain dissatisfied following the outcome of the internal review, you have the right to apply directly to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) for a decision. The ICO can be contacted at www.ico.org.uk.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
foi.requests @museumwales.ac.uk
amgueddfa.cymru | museum.wales

Rhif elusen | Charity number 525774

thread_title: N610CGV — 1924–1930 instruments and any closed parent title (enquiry 261007-6799563)
subject: N610CGV — WA231076 / WA240304 — 1924–1930 instruments and any closed parent title
body:
Mr Haste / Customer Support

Reference: N610CGV
Your letter: 30 July 2026
Also: 260918-6720625; 260919-6726246; 260929-6766714
Titles: WA231076 and WA240304 (closed)
Property: land on the north side of Leckwith Road, Llandough (Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr)

This is not a complaint, not a request to reopen the stage 2 review of 25 May 2026, and not a request that you determine ownership.

I am asking you to search the historic files you have already retrieved and to say whether a 1924–1930 instrument for the house plot is on them.

Family evidence states that John Williams registered the house and garden parcel in 1928, and that an agreement of 15 May 1924 is on the WA231076 file. Llandough was not a compulsory-registration area in 1928. I need to know whether any voluntary first registration, or any filed conveyance or agreement of that date, exists.

Please answer these points, and send copies by email to [redacted] where the document is held:

1. Any title number opened between 1924 and 1930 for this land, including a voluntary first registration in the name of John Williams, and any closed title later absorbed into WA231076 or WA240304. If none, please say none.

2. Historical editions of the register and title plan for WA231076 and WA240304 (form HC1), including the edition of 23 February 1983 already listed in your 30 July letter.

3. The agreement of 15 May 1924, if filed on WA231076 or any parent title, with its plan.

4. Any other filed instrument dated 1924–1930, and any entry for such an instrument on the 1971 abstract of title or the A13-DL list of documents lodged with first registration.

5. If a document in 3 or 4 is not held, please say it is not held, rather than omit it.

If email copies will not be issued, confirm each item is or is not held and give the OC2 / HC1 wording and the postal address so the forms can go in without a further inventory letter.

Please reply to this email.

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: EIR 00210772 — internal review and formal chases
subject: Re: Great House Farm, Llandough – Request 00210772 – Internal Review – Formal Chase – unanswered points from 30 September and 11 September
body:
Information Governance Team
cc: Monitoring Officer; Data Protection Officer

Case Ref 00210772 — Internal Review requested 7 July 2026

This is a formal chase of unanswered points already put to you. It is not a new request and must not be used to restart any clock.

On 11 September 2026 you wrote that service areas had found further historical documentation, that you were still sifting it, and that because some of it is “not necessarily Council documentation but is nonetheless in the Council’s possession” you were considering whether to consult third parties. You said you would try to give a clearer timetable by the end of the following week (i.e. by 18 September 2026).

On 30 September 2026 I asked, by Tuesday 6 October 2026, for:
1. A firm date by which the completed internal review decision will be issued;
2. A non-disclosive description of the further documentation located (date range, creator/supplier, how it came into the Council’s possession, approximate volume);
3. Confirmation that the newly located documentation is being preserved without alteration, destruction or disposal; and
4. Immediate release of any material that can properly be disclosed without awaiting third-party consultation.

None of those four points has been answered.

What you have not said
You have not identified a single document found in the September sift. You have not named any third-party consultee class, the date any consultation was sent, or the date by which a reply was required. You have not stated whether the material is held under EIR or FOIA. You have not addressed the child / personal-data point previously raised. You have not confirmed a preservation hold. Silence on each of these points is itself a recorded position.

What is now required (unchanged from the unanswered requests)
(a) Issue the internal review decision. On any view the ICO’s recommended maximum of 40 working days from the request for review (7 July 2026) has long passed. If you contend that EIR does not apply, say so expressly and identify the statutory basis for treating the request under FOIA alone.

(b) Attach a schedule of every document found in the further search: date, description, format, holding service, whether Council or third-party record in the Council’s possession, and the decision on each (disclose / part-disclose / withhold with the precise regulation or section).

(c) If any third-party consultation has occurred or is proposed, name the class of consultee, the date the consultation was sent, and the deadline set for reply. A consultee’s silence is not a ground to withhold.

(d) Confirm in writing that every document in the sift, and every related planning, enforcement, legal, committee, land, finance and correspondence record (including predecessor-authority material), is under a formal preservation hold and will not be destroyed, weeded, transferred or disposed of while 00210772 and related requests remain open.

(e) Address the child / personal-data point: if any record has been withheld or is being considered for withholding because it mentions a child, identify the record and the exemption. If no such withholding exists, say so expressly. Treat the personal-data element also as a subject-access request under UK GDPR for Sion Hywel Buckler (child occupant in 1988).

The 7 July 2026 answer treated the matter as a planning-register query. That was too narrow. The sift must cover the full list previously set out (planning files including unpublished appendices, enforcement, building control, environmental health, demolition, legal-services files, member/officer correspondence, land/estates files, finance records, and predecessor-authority transfers to Glamorgan Archives).

Public-accountability questions (to be answered from the documents, including those found in September)
1. Was any Council or predecessor expenditure, fee, cost, grant or works associated with the occupation, demolition or redevelopment?
2. Was any Council or predecessor land, right, permission or undertaking involved?
3. Were officers or members told of anything that contradicted or qualified the ownership, occupation, heritage or demolition account then being used?
4. What accounting, audit, legal, planning, committee and correspondence records survive?
5. Was any irregularity, conflict, material error or control failure identified, reported, or formally accounted for?
6. If the Council’s position is that there is nothing to examine, state that expressly and identify the documents relied on.

By return
Within 5 working days: the document schedule, the preservation confirmation, and either the child-exemption notice or a clear statement that none exists.
Within 10 working days: the internal review decision with copies of everything you are able to disclose.

This email records that the four points put to you on 30 September 2026 remain unanswered as of 6 October 2026. If no substantive response is received, the continuing failure to complete the internal review will be referred to the Information Commissioner without further notice.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: RE: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
Dear FOI Team,

FOI 2026-036 – response of 5 October 2026

Thank you for the letter. I note the additional records identified (Ref 13.2 waterwheel and the page of MS 3360/3).

What remains unanswered
On 27 September I corrected the place names in the FOI 2026-032 pack, identifying at least PAS 2022.18.1 (NGR SS9934672805) and a separate Great House Farm entry at Llandow as belonging to different properties. Your reply of 28 September accepted the distinction: the collections system does not group by similar names, no recorded cross-attribution is held, and those hits arose from the search rather than catalogue overlap.

The 5 October letter does not supply a cleaned / filtered schedule showing which of the FOI 2026-032 items survive that filter. Until that is provided, the cross-reference still carries the Cowbridge and Llandow material. That is the point left open on 28 September and still open now.

What you have not said
You have not stated, item by item, which of the earlier schedule entries are now excluded as relating to Great House Farm near Cowbridge or Great House Farm, Llandow. You have not confirmed the parish of the page of MS 3360/3 that you identify as relating to Great House Farm (which Llandough, and any vendor / tenant / acreage / parcel detail that identifies the holding). You have not confirmed whether Ref 13.2 (waterwheel collected 1 April 1979 from “Llandough Farm”, donor Wales and West Housing Association) is recorded as the Penarth site opposite the hospital, or as the farmhouse demolished by BP on 6 December 1988.

Please therefore supply:
1. A filtered schedule of the FOI 2026-032 records that remain after exclusion of all items relating to Great House Farm / Llandough near Cowbridge and to Great House Farm, Llandow. For each surviving entry: accession or archive number, title, date, and one-line description.
2. Explicit parish confirmation for the page of MS 3360/3 identified as relating to Great House Farm: which Llandough, and any vendor / tenant / acreage / parcel detail that identifies the holding.
3. Confirmation whether Ref 13.2 is recorded as the Penarth site opposite the hospital, or as the farmhouse demolished by BP on 6 December 1988.

These are requests for recorded information already within the searches undertaken. I am not seeking new searches or opinions. The unanswered point is the filter that you accepted was necessary on 28 September but have not yet applied in a disclosed schedule.

Cofion,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: RE: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your email.

In relation to the filtered schedule, Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold a separate recorded document identifying, item by item, which search results were excluded following review. Search results were reviewed by staff to determine whether they related to the location specified in your request, and the outcome of that review was reflected in our response of 5 October 2026. We do not hold a separate audit schedule of those decisions.

In relation to MS 3360/3, the relevant page was previously supplied in response to FOI 2026-032. That page records that "Great House" formed part of the Llandough Estate sale particulars of 1924, was occupied by W.G. Thomas & Sons, comprised approximately 202 acres, was situated in the Parish of Llanfair, and describes the homestead as being situated in the Village of Llandough. No additional recorded information identifying the holding has been identified within the material reviewed.

In relation to Ref 13.2, the collections record describes the item as a "Waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)". No further location information has been identified within the record.

We trust this clarifies the position.

thread_title: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: Re: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
FOI Team,

Thank you for the clarification.

Your email of 7 October materially clarifies the position, and I have now corrected my records to distinguish the different Llandough farmsteads.

Ref 13.2 — Llandough Farm opposite the hospital

I understand and accept the distinction in your catalogue description:

“Waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)”

This refers to the separate Llandough Farm in the Llandough near Penarth/Cardiff locality, not to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr. I am not seeking to attribute the waterwheel to Great House Farm.

I will therefore treat Ref 13.2 as a separate Llandough Farm record unless a primary Museum record expressly establishes otherwise.

MS 3360/3 — Great House / Llandough Estate

The more significant clarification is the information you have now supplied from MS 3360/3.

You state that the page records that:

- “Great House” formed part of the Llandough Estate sale particulars of 1924;
- it was occupied by W.G. Thomas & Sons;
- it comprised approximately 202 acres;
- it was situated in the Parish of Llanfair; and
- the homestead was situated in the Village of Llandough.

Those particulars provide a much more specific identification than the earlier catalogue description.

I am particularly interested in the combination of Llandough Estate + Parish of Llanfair + Village of Llandough + approximately 202 acres + W.G. Thomas & Sons.

Could you therefore confirm one narrow point from the record already examined:

Does the MS 3360/3 page or plan itself contain any further recorded identifier which identifies which historical Llandough is meant — for example the specific place-name form, neighbouring farms, estate owner, parish/benefice wording, acreage breakdown, plan number, tenant information, road, church or other geographical feature?

I am not asking the Museum to make a new identification or to provide an opinion. I am asking only whether such information is actually recorded in the page or plan you have already examined.

There is an important reason for keeping this distinction precise. There are two different farmsteads in the Llandough near Penarth/Cardiff locality relevant to the Museum's records:

1. Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, beside St Dochdwy's Church; and
2. Llandough Farm, separately described by the Museum as “opposite hospital”.

They must not be treated as alternative names for one farm.

There is also a separate question concerning the Museum's wording “Llandough Church Farm” in the 1858 provenance of accession 63.24. I now understand that this should not automatically be equated with either of the above merely because it contains the word Llandough. Unless the underlying historical evidence expressly identifies the 1858 “Church Farm”, I will continue to record that identity as unresolved.

Filtered schedule

I also accept your clarification that the Museum does not hold a separate recorded audit schedule showing, item by item, which search results staff excluded after reviewing the results.

I therefore do not ask the Museum to create such a schedule.

For the purposes of the record, I will instead distinguish between:

- records positively identified as Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr;
- records positively identified as the separate Llandough Farm opposite the hospital;
- records from other Llandoughs, including Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge;
- and source-specific records whose location remains unresolved.

The new MS 3360/3 particulars are sufficiently distinctive to make the underlying page and plan an important identification source, so I would be grateful for confirmation of whether any further geographical identifier is actually recorded there.

Thank you again for the clarification.

Cofion,

Sion Buckler

subject: DBS Response to your Subject Access Request (SAR)
body:
Ref: Subject Access Request DPR2026/46503

Dear Mr Buckler,

Please accept our apologies for the delay in responding to your request, Defence Business Services (DBS) Disclosure Team are receiving a high volume of submissions and as such we are experiencing delays in processing requests.

Following receipt of your request on 5th August, for information held about you in accordance with Data Protection Legislation. Please see our response below relating to your Subject Access Request (SAR).

You can download your response using the below link.
https://secureshare.mod.gov.uk/documents/fcc8e7df-f808-46ca-b432-07cb6897bb10
The files will be available for download until 6 November 2026 11:59pm. Please do not access this link if you are not the intended recipient.

You asked for:

I am writing to request information under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 regarding any involvement of UK Armed Forces personnel in mine, my pregnant mother and heart conditioned fathers eviction/dispossession that took place in 1988 at Ty Mawr (Great House Farm), Llandough, near Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan.

Specifically, I request the following:

1. Whether any units of the UK Armed Forces, including but not limited to UK Special Forces (e.g. SAS), were deployed, tasked, or otherwise involved in this incident before, during or after the 1988 eviction (involving upto a reported 30 police officers).

2. Any records, logs, operational reports, orders, requests or communications referring to military support to civil authorities in relation to this event.

3. Any documentation relating to Military Aid to the Civil Authorities (MACA) requests connected to this incident.

4. Any correspondence between the Ministry of Defence and:

+ South Wales Police

+ Vale of Glamorgan Council

+ Welsh Office (as it existed at the time)

concerning the eviction or associated operations.

5. Any internal assessments, reviews, or after-action reports relating to the use of force or military involvement in this case.

For clarity, the incident involved the removal of myself and my family from Ty Mawr (Great House Farm) in 1988, reportedly involving a significant and coordinated enforcement presence.

We have conducted reasonable and proportionate searches for information in relation to yourself at our storage facility and on all Defence Business Services systems using the information you have provided, no information in scope of your request was located.

If you are not satisfied with this response or you wish to complain about any aspect of the handling of your request, then you should contact the Disclosures Team (civilian) in the first instance.  If you remain dissatisfied then you may apply for an independent internal review by contacting the MOD Information Rights Compliance Team, Zone D, Ground Floor, MOD Main Building, Whitehall, SW1A 2HB (e-mail
CIO-DPA@mod.gov.uk).

Alternatively, you can raise a complaint to the Information Commissioner under Section 165 (Complaints by data subjects) of the Data Protection Act 2018.  Further details of the role and powers of the Information Commissioner can be found on the Commissioner's website,
http://www.ico.org.uk.

Please see the Ministry of Defence Privacy Notice
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ministry-of-defence-privacy-notice/mod-privacy-notice. This notice explains your rights and gives you the information that you are entitled to under the Data Protection legislation in response to your Subject Access Request (SAR).

Yours sincerely,
DBS Disclosures Officer 6
Defence Business Services Civilian Disclosures Team
On Behalf of
Jo Turton
DBS Data Protection Lead

thread_title: DPR2026/46503 — internal review of handling and classification (CIO-FOI-IR)
subject: DPR2026/46503 – internal review of handling and classification
body:
Dear MOD Information Rights Compliance Team,

I request an internal review of the handling of my request concerning possible UK Armed Forces involvement in the 1988 eviction of my family from Tý Mawr (Great House Farm), Llandough, near Penarth.

Reference: DPR2026/46503
Response date: 9 October 2026

1. The request appears to have been handled under the wrong legal regime, or only partially answered

My original request expressly invoked the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and sought information about potential military deployment, Military Aid to the Civil Authorities (MACA), operational records, interdepartmental correspondence and the conduct of the eviction. The response instead identifies the matter as a Subject Access Request and states that no information within scope was located.

I recognise that any parts seeking my own personal data may properly be dealt with under data-protection legislation (and a parallel SAR response has been received). However, the request also seeks institutional and operational information that is not limited to my personal data. The Information Commissioner’s guidance states that where a request covers both personal data and other information, the authority should handle the two parts separately under the applicable legal regimes.

Please therefore confirm whether the non-personal and institutional elements of my original request were formally considered under FOIA. If not, please arrange for those elements to be handled as an FOI request, with a substantive response.

2. Clarification of the searches conducted

The response states that searches were conducted at your storage facility and across Defence Business Services systems. Please clarify whether the searches extended to all relevant MOD business areas and historical records within the scope of my request, rather than being confined to the systems described in the letter.

In particular, please review whether appropriate searches were made for:
- Records concerning possible Armed Forces involvement in the 1988 eviction, including any requests for military assistance to civil authorities.
- Correspondence between the MOD and South Wales Police, the Vale of Glamorgan Council and the Welsh Office, as it existed at the time.
- Relevant historical operational, administrative and records-management archives, including any records transferred to an archival repository.
- Records concerning the planning, authorisation, coordination or subsequent review of any military support connected with the incident.

I am not asserting that such records necessarily exist. I am asking that their possible existence be properly investigated and that the scope of the searches be reviewed.

3. No records located is not the same as a determination that no involvement occurred

I understand that the MOD has not located information within the scope of the searches described. I do not interpret that finding as proof that military involvement occurred, nor as proof that it did not occur. My request concerns a specific historical incident and seeks to establish what documentary evidence, if any, survives concerning the authorities involved and the decision-making surrounding the eviction.

If relevant information is not held, please confirm that position under FOIA. If information is held but cannot be disclosed, please identify the applicable exemptions and provide the appropriate decision and explanation.

4. Administrative discrepancies

The response refers to receipt of the request on “05/088/2026”, which is not a valid date, and contains the heading “T5(CH) – 27 Nov 20”. Please confirm the correct date on which the request was received and explain whether the heading is simply a document reference or has any bearing on the handling of this request.

5. Requested outcome

I request:
1. An independent internal review of the handling and classification of the original request.
2. Confirmation that the FOI elements have been separately identified and considered.
3. A review of the adequacy and scope of the searches for relevant historical records.
4. A substantive FOI response addressing the information requested, subject to any applicable statutory exemptions.
5. Confirmation of the applicable review and complaint procedures, and the expected response date for this internal review.

This request is made to establish the documentary facts concerning the 1988 incident. It should not be taken as an allegation that any particular military unit was involved.

Please acknowledge this internal review request and confirm the expected response date.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: Independent Complaints Reviewer — referral ICR/090/26
subject: ICR/090/26 – further formal points on the first-registration file and 1987 amalgamation
body:
Dear Independent Complaints Reviewer,

Reference ICR/090/26.

I hold the stage-one decision of 19 April 2026 and the stage-two decision of 25 May 2026. I also hold the schedule of 43 documents on the first-registration files released on 30 July 2026.

The family’s established case, recorded on the public wiki and under investigation, is that the 1877 arrangement took effect in 1928, transferring the full Parcel A (house and buildings, barn, stable and west-side yard, garden, northern forest and the south-east ground later registered as VG41) to the Williams family. The 1939 agreement/plan depicts Parcel B only. On the family account, the 1949 attempt to make the occupation of Parcel A permissive failed, title papers were reported missing in 1950–52, and Western Ground Rents’ 4 July 1955 enforcement of Parcel B also seized the Parcel-A forest and green under “whole farm” wording. Later documentary work is directed at corroborating or precisely mapping that account and tracing those areas into later titles.

Four specific points remain unanswered and are relevant to that investigation:

1. The 1969 root deed recited as the root of title does not appear on the schedule. Please confirm whether HMLR holds that deed under any other reference, or whether it was never lodged.
2. What evidence exists on the file of notice or opportunity to object given to the occupying family (Williams / Buckler) in 1982–83.
3. The precise legal and administrative basis for the 1987 title amalgamation that took place while the Court of Appeal proceedings in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler were still live.
4. Whether the inclusion of the woodland (or any land beyond the 1938 conveyance) is regarded as a possible mistake capable of alteration or indemnity under the Land Registration Act 2002 and Practice Guide 39.

Please confirm these points form part of the live investigation and state the exact start date of the ICR six-month period (so that the ~25 November 2026 outer limit can be verified).

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: FOI 1264/26 — non-personal operational records, November–December 1988
subject: FOI/EIR request — non-personal operational records concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, November–December 1988
body:
Dear South Wales Police Information Rights Team,

Please treat this as a request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 for recorded information, excluding personal data and excluding any material for which the appropriate handling route is the separate subject-access request already open. The site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy’s Church, Cardiff (approx. ST 168 733), and the period is 1 November to 31 December 1988 inclusive.

Please search the relevant South Wales Constabulary / predecessor-force and successor holdings, including any transferred records available to the Force, for existing non-personal records that refer to the site or the events associated with its possession and demolition. Relevant record types, if held, include:
1. incident or occurrence logs and control-room records;
2. deployment, duty or operational logs and any record identifying whether officers attended;
3. correspondence between police, the local authority, landowner/developer, court enforcement officers or other public bodies about the site;
4. any recorded liaison or request for police assistance connected with possession, eviction, demolition, public order or the handling of complaints; and
5. records-transfer, retention or disposal entries for the relevant operational record series, if the responsive records are no longer held.

I am not asserting that a police deployment or a particular incident record necessarily exists. If no responsive record is located, please state that result and identify, so far as reasonably practicable, the record systems, index/series, date range and site/name variants searched. Please distinguish “not found in the systems searched” from a contemporaneous record showing that a file was destroyed or transferred. If transferred, please identify the receiving repository and reference where recorded. If any information is withheld, identify the specific statutory basis and release reasonably separable non-exempt information.

The existing SAR and internal review under ref. 719/26 are separate processes. If a record contains personal data, please do not disclose it through this FOI route; please identify it only as necessary to explain the FOIA decision and continue to handle personal data through the live SAR. This FOI request is not asking South Wales Police to determine ownership or to decide whether an offence occurred.

Please confirm receipt, the request reference, and the statutory response date.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: RE: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
Dear FOI Team,

FOI 2026-036 — your letter of 7 October 2026

Thank you. I note three points from that letter.

1. You do not hold a separate recorded document listing, item by item, which search results were excluded. Please state which systems were searched for that schedule (collections database, search-export, review log, email, paper file) and whether a physical file was retrieved, and by whom and on what date. A not-held answer is incomplete without that (FOIA s.16).

2. MS 3360/3: the page already supplied records Great House as part of the 1924 Llandough Estate sale particulars, occupied by W.G. Thomas & Sons, about 202 acres, Parish of Llanfair, homestead in the Village of Llandough. Please confirm whether the catalogue or the page itself names which Llandough (Llandough-juxta-Penarth or Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge). If that is not on the page or in the catalogue entry, say so.

3. Ref 13.2 is recorded as a waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital). I treat that as the Penarth hospital site, not the farmhouse demolished on 6 December 1988, unless a further recorded field says otherwise.

I am not asking for a new search or for a document you say you do not hold. I am asking for the systems searched and the physical-file check on the not-held point, and the parish identification if it is already on the page or catalogue entry.

Cofion,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: FOI2026/09019 — clarification of the non-Special-Forces remainder
subject: FOI2026/09019 — clarification of the non-Special-Forces remainder and existing retention/search records
body:
Dear Ministry of Defence FOI Team,

I am writing about FOI2026/09019 and the related outstanding correspondence. I understand that the Ministry relied on section 23(5) in relation to Special Forces material. This message does not ask you to confirm or deny whether Special Forces information is held. I am narrowing the outstanding information request to non-Special-Forces information that can be considered separately, without prejudicing the current internal review or the related subject-access request.

For Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and the period 1 November–31 December 1988, please disclose any recorded information held by non-Special-Forces parts of the Ministry concerning:
1. any request, assessment or record of Military Aid to the Civil Authorities (MACA) relating to the location or relevant events;
2. any incident, deployment, duty-log, correspondence or administrative record held by regular Army, Territorial Army or Royal Military Police units that records activity relating to that location and period; and
3. any existing search record, case note, retention schedule, transfer list or disposal entry that explains how the non-Special-Forces portion of FOI2026/09019 was searched or what happened to potentially responsive records.

Please identify, at a level that can properly be disclosed, which non-Special-Forces departments, record systems, date ranges and catalogue/file series were searched for these points. Where responsive information is not held, please distinguish the result of a search from a record showing prior destruction, transfer or disposal; if a transfer or disposal entry exists, provide its date, reference and destination where recorded.

Please process any severable non-exempt information without treating the section 23(5) response on Special Forces as applying automatically to every non-Special-Forces record. If this narrower scope needs a new reference under your process, please tell me and register only the genuinely new element as a separate request; please do not restart or close the existing request or internal review as a result of this clarification.

This is an information request, not a request for the Ministry to decide title or the merits of any civil proceedings. It also does not ask you to disclose personal data through FOIA; the separate subject-access route remains separate.

Please confirm receipt and the applicable response date for any part registered as a new request.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread_title: Cadw — ATISN 27021: records behind the 1988 listing-file disposal finding (October 2026)
subject: ATISN 27021 — existing records behind the 1988 listing-file disposal finding
body:
Dear Cadw / Welsh Government Complaints Manager and Chief Inspector,

I refer to the internal-review outcomes of 2, 10 and 29 July 2026 and the Chief Inspector’s letters of 27 August and 4 September 2026 concerning the 1988 Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr listing file for Llandough-juxta-Penarth.

The previous responses said the file had “most likely” been destroyed, that no destruction record could be found, and that Cadw could not say what retention arrangements applied 38 years ago. I am not asking you to repeat the response or recreate a record that does not exist. I ask whether any pre-existing recorded information remains that supports or qualifies the “most likely destroyed” conclusion or documents the file’s lifecycle.

Please disclose any existing file inventory, closure note, archive catalogue entry, transfer list, disposal authority, retention schedule, weeding/destruction record, archival receipt, email/minute/note recording the search or basis for the conclusion, or record showing whether the file remained held or was transferred on/after 6 December 1988. Please provide the recorded date and responsible role/unit for any documented disposal or transfer decision.

If no additional record is held, please distinguish an actual contemporaneous disposal decision/log from the present-day inability to locate the file. Identify repositories, indices and systems searched for this focused request. If any information is withheld, cite the statutory basis and disclose reasonably separable information.

Please preserve any extant records within scope while the related complaint and disclosure routes remain active. This is a request for recorded information, not a request to decide title, possession or the legal effect of the 1987 proceedings. This is a focused request for additional recorded information, not an appeal or a request to reopen the merits of the earlier complaint. If it falls outside the scope or closure status of ATISN 27021, please register it as a new FOI request, cross-reference ATISN 27021 for context, and confirm the new reference and statutory response date. If you consider the requested material already covered by the earlier request/response, please identify the precise part of the prior request/response that dealt with each category and tell me how the additional points will be handled.

Yours faithfully,
Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

thread_title: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request
subject: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request — Council-held planning, heritage and public-authority record for Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr, Llandough
body:
Democratic and Scrutiny Services
Vale of Glamorgan Council
Democratic@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

cc: FoiUnit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk (for information only — this is not a new FOI request)

Dear Democratic and Scrutiny Services,

Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / request for a focused Task and Finish Review

I am a resident with a long-standing family connection to Great House Farm (Tÿ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth. A public documentary archive of the site is maintained at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

I request that the Council consider a focused Scrutiny Topic Suggestion leading to a Task and Finish Review (or other appropriate scrutiny mechanism) concerning the Council-held planning, heritage, environmental and public-authority record relating to Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr / Church View Close.

Proposed scope (within the Council’s remit):

• the Council-held planning, heritage, environmental and public-authority record relating to Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr / Church View Close;
• the chronology of Council decisions, records and responses from the mid-twentieth century onwards;
• identification of missing, contradictory or unresolved Council-held records and, where appropriate, referral to the body with the relevant jurisdiction;
• consideration of the site’s heritage and historical record, including its proposed interpretation in the Tÿ Mawr replica museum project in Puerto Madryn, Chubut; and
• recommendations within the Council’s powers, without asking the Council to determine private title, criminal liability or matters reserved to courts or other public bodies.

This is an evidence-review and accountability route. It is not a request for the Council to decide private title or liability.

I am happy to complete the online Scrutiny Topic Suggestion Form if preferred, or to supply any further information the Democratic Services team requires.

Please acknowledge receipt and indicate the process and timescale for consideration.

Kind regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

body:
Dear Mr Buckler,

Many thanks for your e-mail below and your request for Scrutiny to consider the topic suggested as part of it's Task and Finish work.

Unfortunately, on this occasion we will be unable to consider the request for several reasons:

1. The purpose of Task and Finish is to review existing policy Council considerations and identify areas for future policy direction at a strategic level impacting on a county wide basis. These topics are purposefully strategic in manner, and are based upon areas that Committees determine to have the most positive impact.

2. In addition to the above, the purpose of Scrutiny is not to review evidence related to individual historical decisions and make subsequent recommendations, particularly related to planning, which should be navigated through other channels.

3. We are aware through other correspondence to which you have copied us into that there are ongoing concerns being raised through a variety of channels including Welsh Government, CADW, MSs and MPs, and as such it would not be appropriate for a Scrutiny Task and Finish to add an additional layer of stakeholders and complexity in exploring the issues; notwithstanding points 1 and 2 raised.

Kind Regards,
James

thread_title: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: RE: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
Mr Buckler

Thank you for your email.

In relation to the "filtered schedule", as previously explained, Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold a separate recorded document identifying, item by item, which search results were excluded following review. The review was undertaken by staff using the records and search results identified during the handling of the request. No separate audit schedule, review log or equivalent record of exclusion decisions was created.

In relation to MS 3360/3, following further review we have confirmed that the page previously supplied does not relate to the property that was the subject of FOI 2026-036. While the document refers to a property known as "Great House", it relates to a holding in the Parish of Llanfair and not to Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Llandough (near Penarth/Cardiff), which was the subject of your request. The document should therefore be regarded as outside the scope of FOI 2026-036.

We do not hold any further recorded information linking MS 3360/3 to Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Llandough (near Penarth/Cardiff).

In relation to Ref 13.2, our position remains unchanged. The collections record describes the item as a "Waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)". No further location information has been identified within that record.

We have no further recorded information to provide in relation to these matters.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
foi.requests @museumwales.ac.uk
amgueddfa.cymru | museum.wales
